Files are written only at waf.py:145-155, so in single-region scope BOTH the REGIONAL data already collected is lost and run_module prints 'waf module failed'. The --all global phase (main.py:145, scope CLOUDFRONT, with the us-east-1 session from main.py:221) has the same problem. WAF data has no consumer in policy_parser.py or the dashboard (grep for waf/web_acls finds none), so the accuracy impact is small. The high rating comes from case A: out-of-scope API calls with credentials the operator did not intend to use, and cross-account data contamination in the deliverable.
evidence: waf.py:32 `region_session = session.__class__(profile_name=session.profile_name, region_name="us-east-1")`; waf.py:34 `client = region_session.client("wafv2")` unguarded. Offline repro using the real waf.enumerate with stubbed client methods (scratchpad/agents/collectors-core-2/waf_repro.py). Case A, env key plus a [default] profile with a different key: client sessions (region, key) = [('eu-west-2', <ENV key>), ('us-east-1', <DEFAULT-PROFILE key>)]. Case B, no profiles: 'waf raised: ProfileNotFound The config profile (default) could not be found'; files written: [] (the REGIONAL pass had already succeeded).
impact: The operator unknowingly enumerates a different AWS account or principal (a scope violation, with CloudTrail entries in an unintended account) and ships that account's WAF configuration inside another client's report. Otherwise WAF output disappears entirely for Docker, CI and env-credential users.
fix: Reuse the existing credentials: `client = session.client("wafv2", region_name="us-east-1")` (boto3 Session.client accepts region_name; checked locally). Wrap client creation and each scope in try/except. Write partial results per scope, or write in a finally block, so one scope's failure does not discard the other.

title: Module failures are swallowed: exit code 0 even when every module fails, and the manifest has no per-module status
explanation: run_module (app/main.py:89-98) catches Exception and only prints it. main() returns None; the script entry point (main.py:288-289) and the console script (pyproject.toml:33 app.main:main) therefore exit 0. generate_manifest (main.py:47-86) lists directories that exist on disk as 'modules_executed' and records no success, error or denied status. A module that wrote an error stub still counts as executed, and one that crashed before makedirs is silently missing. The collectors encode errors in several incompatible ways: safe() returns a default such as [] (aws_utils.py:19-33); lambda_.py:59-63 writes {'Error':...} in place of the list; cloudtrail.py:10 describe_trails is unguarded, so no file is written; k8s _safe_call writes {'error':...}. The policy_parser loaders treat non-lists as empty (e.g. policy_parser.py:1152, :1690). A non-zero exit happens only when an error occurs outside run_module: STS get_caller_identity at start-up, get_enabled_regions, or makedirs. enum.sh's success count (enum.sh:76-85) therefore catches up-front auth failures but none of the partial failures. 'Meaningless' overstates it slightly.
evidence: Scratch repro (repro_exitcode.py): every collector and policy_parser.analyze patched to raise ClientError(ExpiredToken) and main() run in a subprocess. Output: `exit code: 0`, `failed lines: 31`, manifest run_metadata keys = [account_id, mode, region, regions_enumerated, caller_arn, caller_user_id, timestamp_start, timestamp_end, duration_seconds], `modules_executed: []`.
impact: An empty service cannot be told apart from a denied or crashed one. In long --all runs with static temporary credentials that expire partway through, later regions come out empty while the run still 'succeeds'. The graph silently loses paths, and automation such as batch wrappers or CI cannot detect partial runs.
fix: Have run_module return or record a status object with label, ok/error, exception class, message and duration. Collect these into a `module_status` list in manifest.json. Make safe() raise or record AccessDenied/ExpiredToken in a shared per-run error registry instead of returning [] silently. Standardise the error stub format, e.g. `{"_error": {...}}` beside the data file. Exit with sys.exit(main()) returning a non-zero code (e.g. 2) when any module fails, and abort early on ExpiredToken.

title: No module selection or K8s opt-out: cluster-wide Kubernetes enumeration (including list secrets) runs automatically against every EKS cluster
explanation: k8s.enumerate runs unconditionally after eks in both modes (app/main.py:113 single-region, :161 per region). parse_args (main.py:182-190) offers only --region/--all/--zip/--dashboard/--port, with no --modules, --skip or --no-k8s. For every cluster in eks/clusters.json that has an endpoint and CA (k8s.py:206-217), it authenticates with the caller's IAM identity and lists namespaces, pods, service accounts, RBAC, secrets, services and ingresses cluster-wide (k8s.py:95-172). Secrets are listed with core_v1.list_secret_for_all_namespaces() (k8s.py:146). The Kubernetes list API returns full V1Secret objects including .data; the client deserialises them into memory even though only name, namespace, type and annotations are saved (k8s.py:147-156). The docstring's 'names only' is true for disk output only. These calls appear in EKS control-plane audit logs when enabled and can trigger GuardDuty EKS findings. A related point the reviewers did not raise: pods are saved in full via to_dict() (k8s.py:103-105), so plaintext env-var secrets in pod specs land in the report.
evidence: app/main.py:113 `run_module("k8s", k8s.enumerate, session, f"{base_path}/eks", f"{base_path}/k8s")`; :161 same for region_path; app/components/k8s.py:145-157 `secrets = core_v1.list_secret_for_all_namespaces().items`; parse_args main.py:182-190 has no service selection.
impact: Operators whose rules of engagement exclude workload-plane access, or who need a low footprint, cannot avoid the noisiest action in the run. Secret values cross the wire into process memory, and every API call is attributed to their IAM identity in cluster audit logs.
fix: Add --modules/--skip (comma lists) and a --no-k8s flag; consider making K8s opt-in (--k8s). For secrets, request metadata only: list with header `Accept: application/json;as=PartialObjectMetadataList;g=meta.k8s.io;v=v1` via api_client.call_api, or use the metadata API, so values are never transferred. Redact env values in pods.json, or save only env var names and valueFrom references.

title: Report path keyed only by date+account; stale files from earlier runs persist and the analyzer's sibling-dir fallback imports other regions' data into single-region analysis
explanation: Output paths are reports/<YYYYMMDD>/<account>[/<region>] (main.py:215, 260), created with exist_ok=True and with no run id or principal. Collectors overwrite only the files they write. generate_manifest walks whatever is on disk (main.py:52-65), and make_archive zips the whole folder (main.py:252-255, 278-281). A run by a different principal in the same account on the same day overwrites some files and leaves others. The manifest records only the last caller_arn. Stale k8s/<cluster>/ dirs persist. A stale eks/clusters.json survives only when eks.enumerate raises a non-ClientError: on ClientError it overwrites the file with {"Error"} (eks.py:39-43), so that sub-claim is narrower than stated. The reviewer missed a stronger mechanism. In single-region mode the policy_parser loaders fall back to sibling directories whenever the local region has no data: _load_ec2_data when instances.json is empty (policy_parser.py:1152, 1166-1190), and _load_k8s_data when no clusters are found (:3266-3275, `if not clusters:`). A single-region run of region A on the same day as an earlier run of region B therefore imports B's instances and EKS clusters into A's analysis and produces edges for resources that are not in A's report. A stale single-region iam/, analysis/ and manifest.json inside an --all region folder also ships in the zip. The dashboard picks the first path ending in manifest.json as the root (index.html:943-949), so a wrong root is theoretically possible, though make_archive writes the top-level manifest first.
evidence:
main.py:215 `account_path = f"reports/{date_today}/{account_number}"`; main.py:260 `base_path = f"reports/{date_today}/{account_number}/{args.region}"`; policy_parser.py:1151-1153 local-or-siblings branch; policy_parser.py:3266-3275 `if not clusters:` sibling scan.
Repro (scratchpad/agents/arch-packaging-ci-2/stale.py): account dir holds region-b (earlier run: 1 instance with an instance profile, 1 EKS cluster) and region-a (current run: instances.json=[], clusters.json=[]). Output:
  _load_ec2_data instances: ['i-b']
  _load_k8s_data clusters: ['cl-b']
  region-a ec2_relationships edges: [('i-b', '...:role/r1', 'INSTANCE_ROLE')]
Count only: 15 of 30 account-level folders under reports/ are not 12-digit account IDs, which suggests manual renaming.
impact: The single-region graph can contain edges and findings for resources from other regions or from older runs, with no indication of where they came from. Reports from two principals or two modes mix silently, and the manifest and zip present them as one run. Analysts can chase stale or out-of-scope paths, or attribute access to the wrong principal.
fix: Write each run to a unique directory, e.g. reports/<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>-<run-id>/<account>/..., or refuse a non-empty target unless --overwrite is passed, and record the caller ARN in the folder name or manifest. In policy_parser, remove the implicit sibling fallback: pass mode and region paths explicitly from main() (single-region means local only; --all means the listed region dirs from this run). Have generate_manifest list only modules the run executed.

title: --all region discovery (ec2:DescribeRegions in us-east-1) is unguarded; a denial, SCP or non-commercial partition crashes the run after the global phase with no manifest or zip
explanation: main.py:221 hard-codes get_boto3_session("us-east-1") for the global phase and region discovery. main.py:227 calls get_enabled_regions() outside run_module, and aws_utils.py:36-42 has no try/except. Any ClientError (UnauthorizedOperation, a region-deny SCP on us-east-1, or invalid credentials for a GovCloud/China partition when run with --region us-gov-west-1 --all) propagates out of main(). The global data is already on disk, but no regional data, manifest.json or zip is produced. The bundled app/utils/regions.json is never used as a fallback; it has no code references.
evidence:
main.py:221 `global_session = get_boto3_session("us-east-1")`; main.py:227 `regions = get_enabled_regions(global_session)` (not wrapped); aws_utils.py:38-42 direct describe_regions call.
Repro (scratchpad/agents/arch-packaging-ci-2/regions_fail.py): main() with --all --zip, all collectors stubbed, describe_regions raising ClientError UnauthorizedOperation. Output:
  main() raised: ClientError ... DescribeRegions operation: denied
  manifest written: False | zip written: False
impact: Least-privilege or leaked credentials without ec2:DescribeRegions, region-locked organisations, and GovCloud/China users get a traceback and a partial, unpackaged report from --all. Red teams with narrow keys are the most likely to hit this.
fix: Wrap discovery in try/except (BotoCoreError, ClientError). On failure, fall back to session.get_available_regions('ec2', partition_name=<partition from caller ARN>) or regions.json, and warn. Derive the global region from the caller ARN partition (aws gives us-east-1, aws-us-gov gives us-gov-west-1, aws-cn gives cn-north-1). Add a --regions a,b,c override. Generate the manifest in a finally block so partial runs are still described.

title: No test suite and no pre-merge CI; most of the shipped collectors and analysers have never been run
explanation: `git ls-files` (89 files) contains no tests/ folder, no test_*.py and no pytest/tox config. The only workflow (.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml) triggers on push to main (:3-5) and its steps are checkout, version, login, buildx, build-and-push and git tag (:21-61). There is no PR trigger and no test, lint or type-check step. PR #14, which added about 2,830 lines (16 collectors plus 5 analysers in policy_parser), is already in origin/main. Merge latency, measured from commit timestamps as merge time minus the PR head commit time: #3-#14 merged in 30-220 s except #4 (about 2 h); #1 and #2 were slower, so 11 of 14 were under 4 minutes, as claimed. Across the 20 local field manifests, 16 collector folders never appear (kms, ecs, cloudformation, glue, codebuild, sagemaker, sns, sqs, ecr, rds, dynamodb, apigateway, cognito, ebs, elb, route53). The kms, compute, messaging, newsurface and extra analysis files never appear either. Missing tests are a process gap rather than a defect, but they let the high-severity --all ordering regression and never-executed code reach :latest.
evidence: `git ls-files | grep -i test` returns nothing; docker-publish.yml:3-5 `on: push: branches: [main]`. A local scan of reports/*/manifest.json (20 runs; counts only) found 16 collectors never present. Analysis files seen: findings 20, permission_map 20, trust 20, summary 20, s3 12, ec2 9, k8s 4, secrets 2, lambda 1; kms, compute, messaging, newsurface and extra 0.
impact: Accuracy regressions in the attack graph (e.g. empty regional edges in --all) ship straight to the Docker :latest image and to pipx users, unnoticed. Half the collectors have never touched a real API response shape.
fix: Add pytest with fixture-based tests. Start with: each collector against botocore Stubber or moto responses; policy_parser.analyze on synthetic report trees in single and --all layouts; an end-to-end main() --all test with patched collectors. Add a `pull_request` + `push` workflow that runs ruff and pytest, and make the Docker publish job `needs:` it. Optionally add an iam-vulnerable-style privesc fixture set as a benchmark.
also_reported_as: No tests/lint/CI checks; shared safe()/save_json helpers used by only 3 collectors, so error conventions diverge

title: Untracked engagement artefacts (tmp, enum.sh) are not in the repo .gitignore and are one `git add .` from a public push; history already holds an org SSO script
explanation: The project section of .gitignore (lines 49-50) adds only `reports`. `git status --porcelain --ignored` shows `?? tmp`, `?? enum.sh`, `?? docs/features.md` and `?? internal-docs/` as untracked and not ignored. tmp contains 2 distinct 12-digit account IDs, 3 STS and 2 IAM ARNs and 1 email address, plus STS/assume-role snippets (counted, not printed). enum.sh hard-codes 6 profile|regions targets (enum.sh:17-24). .claude/settings.local.json is ignored only by the user's global ~/.config/git/ignore:1, so a clone on another machine would not ignore it. There is no .dockerignore, so local `docker build .` sends reports/, tmp, enum.sh, .venv and .git to the build context. The Dockerfile COPYs only requirements.txt and app/, so none of it reaches the image layers. History: commit 228994c added scripts/docker-run.sh, removed in 51c9147. It contains an org-specific aws-sso invocation with a profile, a `printenv | grep -iE 'AWS_SESSION|AWS_SECRET|AWS_ACCESS'` that echoes credentials to the terminal (it did not commit the credentials), and `-e KEY=$VAL` passing. P1-184's point that reports are world-readable (all 4,566 report files are other-readable, umask 022) is real but belongs with P1-025. reports/ itself is gitignored, so it is not at risk of being committed.
evidence: .gitignore:49-50 `# PROJECT BASED` / `reports`; git check-ignore -v: reports -> .gitignore:50; .claude/settings.local.json -> ~/.config/git/ignore:1; tmp and enum.sh not ignored. `ls .dockerignore` -> No such file. `git show 228994c -- scripts/docker-run.sh` lines 17-23 (values redacted).
impact: A routine `git add -A` while adding the untracked docs (docs/features.md, internal-docs/) would publish client account IDs, role names and an operator email to a public repository. The earlier docker-run.sh commit shows this kind of slip has already happened once.
fix: Add to .gitignore: `tmp`, `enum.sh` (or a `local/` or `*.local.*` convention), `.claude/settings.local.json`, `*.zip`, and internal-docs/ if that is private. Move engagement wrappers outside the repo. Add a .dockerignore (reports/, tmp, enum.sh, .git, .venv, .claude, internal-docs, build, *.egg-info). Add a pre-commit gitleaks or detect-secrets hook with a custom rule for 12-digit account IDs and arn:aws patterns. Decide whether 228994c needs a history rewrite with git filter-repo.

title: Field guide and README describe graph edges, paths, weights and dashboard behaviour that the tool does not produce
explanation:
I checked every sub-claim against the code and all of them hold. The two reports describe the same root cause: the operator-facing docs were never reconciled with the graph semantics in policy_parser.py and index.html, and they overlap on CAN_ASSUME_CROSS_ACCOUNT and PUBLIC_INBOUND/INTERNET_FACING.
(1) PUBLIC_INBOUND and INTERNET_FACING appear only as weight keys (policy_parser.py:245-246) and colours (index.html:817). No code path emits them. The real signals are the findings EC2-EXPOSURE-001 and EC2-INET-001 (policy_parser.py:1483, 1504). attack_paths.md:80 calls them 'INTERNET_FACING + PUBLIC_INBOUND findings', and :395-396 lists them as edges.
(2) attack_paths.md:419 names CAN_ASSUME_CROSS_ACCOUNT, but the dashboard emits CAN_ASSUME_CROSS (index.html:1227). That edge is also unreachable in practice. nodeIds is fixed at index.html:1161 and holds only the scanned account's users, roles, groups, policies, instances and buckets, so a foreign-account principal never matches nodeIds.has() at :1218.
(3) The Scenario 2 path pod->IN_CLUSTER->cluster->NODE_ROLE->role (attack_paths.md:151) cannot occur. NODE_ROLE starts at nodegroup:{cluster}/{ng} (policy_parser.py:3326-3335), and nothing emits a cluster->nodegroup edge. The cluster node only gets CLUSTER_ROLE, which points at the cluster service role.
(4) 'sts:AssumeRole on * -> follow CAN_ASSUME edges' (attack_paths.md:78, :176) is misleading. CAN_ASSUME comes only from trust policies whose principal is the exact ARN of an existing user or role node (index.html:1211-1230). The identity-policy side is never used, and the common trust on arn:aws:iam::ACCT:root produces no edge. That is exactly the case 'sts:AssumeRole on *' needs. The finding that actually fires is DANGER-005 (policy_parser.py:161-163).
(5) The weight table (attack_paths.md:37-45) and readme.md:33 say 'direct = 0'. The dashboard turns every 0 into 1: Dijkstra uses `edge.data('weight') || 1` (index.html:2288, :2785), S3 edges use `edge.weight || 1` (:1314), and dashboard-built INSTANCE_ROLE gets 1 (:1243). Weight-0 edges such as FULL_ACCESS, EC2_FULL_ACCESS and POOL_UNAUTH_ROLE therefore cost more than CAN_ADMIN/CAN_CONNECT at 0.5. No PassRole edge exists, so 'PassRole chains = 2' never applies. 'cross-account = 4' applies only to the unreachable CAN_ASSUME_CROSS.
(6) attack_paths.md:20 promises a '📖 attack path link on the node'. Findings are attached only to user, role and group nodes (index.html:1063, 1085, 1111), so non-IAM findings never appear on any node. That covers bucket/, instance/, lambda/, elb/, cognito/, rds/, pod/ and others. This includes every 'Dashboard signal' finding in Scenario 6 (attack_paths.md:257-267). The sidebar shows counts only (index.html:634-641, 2236-2240).
(7) readme.md:35 says Owned nodes are used to 'find paths from them'. Owned marking only toggles a CSS class and a list (index.html:2662-2715). Discover All Paths uses every user, role and instance as a source (:2768-2771) and ignores the owned set.
These are documentation errors and do not change the graph. They are rated medium because they create false negatives in an operator's reasoning: 'no PUBLIC_INBOUND edge, so not exposed', 'no CAN_ASSUME, so no role chaining', and 'my pod reaches the node role via the cluster'.
evidence:
Synthetic run with mocked _load_ec2_data and _load_k8s_data (scratchpad agents/docs/repro_edges.py), for an instance with a public IP, an SG open to 0.0.0.0/0, an IGW route and IMDSv1:
  EC2 edge types: ['HAS_SG', 'INSTANCE_ROLE']
  EC2 finding ids: ['EC2-EXPOSURE-001','EC2-IMDS-001','EC2-INET-001']
  K8s edges: cluster:c1 -CLUSTER_ROLE-> svc role; nodegroup:c1/ng1 -NODE_ROLE-> node role; pod -IN_CLUSTER-> cluster; pod -RUNS_AS-> sa
  cluster->nodegroup edges: 0
Node replay of the exact index.html:1211-1230 loop with trusts {same-acct :root, same-acct role ARN, other-acct :root, other-acct role}: output is only '...role/Src->...role/TgtArn:CAN_ASSUME'. Also `0||1 = 1`.
Across the 3 most recent local runs (anonymised), PUBLIC_INBOUND and INTERNET_FACING edges = 0.
impact: Red and blue teams following the field guide look for edges and paths that never render. They may conclude an instance is not internet-reachable, or that no role chaining is possible, when a role trusts the account root and the principal holds sts:AssumeRole on *. Path costs shown in the UI do not match the documented weight model. Public-resource findings that the guide tells users to look for on nodes are never displayed.
fix:
Docs: in attack_paths.md, remove PUBLIC_INBOUND and INTERNET_FACING from the edge table. Rewrite :80 to reference EC2-EXPOSURE-001 and EC2-INET-001. Rename CAN_ASSUME_CROSS_ACCOUNT to CAN_ASSUME_CROSS and note that it only appears when the external principal is a graph node. Replace 'follow CAN_ASSUME' for sts:AssumeRole * with DANGER-005, plus a note that root-trust roles have no edge. Change the Scenario 2 path to nodegroup->NODE_ROLE, or add a cluster->nodegroup edge in policy_parser (an IN_CLUSTER-style edge from nodegroup to cluster). Fix the weight table and readme.md:33, and reword the 📖 and Owned claims.
Code (preferred, small): replace `|| 1` with `?? 1` at index.html:1314, 2288 and 2785. Attach findings to all node types by indexing findingsMap by entity_arn/node id. Either emit the exposure edges (e.g. principal:internet -> instance) or drop the dead weight keys. Optionally seed Discover All Paths from the owned set when it is non-empty.

title: Inconsistent privesc severities: Attach*Policy HIGH vs Put*Policy CRITICAL; AddUserToGroup fixed MEDIUM
explanation: PRIVESC-003/004/005 (Put*Policy) are CRITICAL (:41-55), while PRIVESC-006/007/008 (Attach*Policy) are HIGH (:57-70). Attaching the AWS-managed AdministratorAccess policy, which always exists, is as direct a path to admin as writing an inline admin policy. PRIVESC-012 AddUserToGroup is a fixed MEDIUM (:88). The engine already holds group effective statements, so it could raise the severity when an admin-equivalent group exists. Similar inconsistencies exist among the PassRole rules: Lambda/EC2/CFN are CRITICAL, ECS/Glue/CodeBuild/SageMaker are HIGH. None of these ratings change detection, only prioritisation.
evidence: Rule table dump: PRIVESC-003/004/005 CRITICAL; PRIVESC-006/007/008 HIGH; PRIVESC-012 MEDIUM; PRIVESC-014/015/016 CRITICAL; PRIVESC-017..020 HIGH.
impact: Distorted triage. Equivalent direct-to-admin paths are ranked differently, and AddUserToGroup into an admin group is under-ranked.
fix: Set Attach*Policy to CRITICAL, or downgrade it only when a Condition such as iam:PolicyARN restricts it, once conditions are parsed. Compute PRIVESC-012 severity dynamically: CRITICAL if any group matched by the resource has DANGER-001/002, otherwise MEDIUM. Align the PassRole rule severities, or derive them from the privilege of the target role (see P1-090).

title: PassRole combo rules accept incomplete chains: PRIVESC-017 fires on RegisterTaskDefinition alone (and the same pattern affects 014/018/019)
explanation: PRIVESC-017's actions_any is [ecs:RunTask, ecs:StartTask, ecs:RegisterTaskDefinition] (:118). RegisterTaskDefinition only registers a definition and cannot run code. ecs:CreateService and ecs:UpdateService are missing, so PassRole+CreateService does not fire. The PassRole + RegisterTaskDefinition + UpdateService path is detected only because RegisterTaskDefinition happens to be in the list. The claim is accurate and the problem is broader. actions_any treats any single step as a complete chain elsewhere too: PRIVESC-014 fires on PassRole + lambda:CreateFunction without any invoke or trigger permission, PRIVESC-018 on PassRole + glue:CreateJob without StartJobRun/CreateTrigger, and PRIVESC-019 on PassRole + codebuild:CreateProject without StartBuild. PRIVESC-014/018/019 also wrongly require PassRole for UpdateFunctionCode, UpdateDevEndpoint and StartBuild, which hijack existing resources and need no PassRole (see P1-095).
evidence: Synthetic results: [iam:PassRole, ecs:RegisterTaskDefinition] gives ['PRIVESC-017']. [iam:PassRole, ecs:CreateService] gives [] (only DANGER-006). [iam:PassRole, ecs:RegisterTaskDefinition, ecs:UpdateService] gives ['PRIVESC-017']. In the condition test, PassRole + lambda:CreateFunction/glue:CreateJob/codebuild:CreateProject fired 014/018/019.
impact: Moderate false-positive rate on deploy and CI roles that can register or create but not execute. Real CreateService paths are missed when RegisterTaskDefinition is absent. Severity is low because most such roles also hold the execute action.
fix: Model each technique as a list of required step-sets (all-of), for example ECS: PassRole AND RegisterTaskDefinition AND any(RunTask, StartTask, CreateService, UpdateService); also PassRole AND any(RunTask, StartTask) with a taskRoleArn override. Lambda: PassRole AND CreateFunction AND any(InvokeFunction, CreateEventSourceMapping, AddPermission/CreateFunctionUrlConfig). Glue: PassRole AND CreateJob AND any(StartJobRun, CreateTrigger). CodeBuild: PassRole AND CreateProject AND any(StartBuild, StartBuildBatch). Move the existing-resource actions (UpdateFunctionCode, UpdateDevEndpoint, StartBuild) into PassRole-free rules.

title: Docs list PUBLIC_INBOUND / INTERNET_FACING as edge types that the engine never emits
explanation: Confirmed: EC2_ACCESS_WEIGHTS declares PUBLIC_INBOUND and INTERNET_FACING (:245-246), and index.html:817 has colours for them. No edges.append in policy_parser.py and no makeEdge call in index.html uses these types. Exposure is reported only as findings EC2-EXPOSURE-001 (:1483) and EC2-INET-001 (:1504). docs/attack_paths.md:395-396 list them in the Edge Type Reference, and :80 calls them findings under names that do not exist. Refuted sub-claim: readme.md:33 'cross-account = 4' is not drift. It matches the dashboard's CAN_ASSUME_CROSS trust edge weight (index.html:1226 `const weight = trust.is_cross_account ? 4 : 2;`). S3 GRANTS_CROSS_ACCOUNT=2 is a different edge type, so the README is at worst incomplete, not wrong.
evidence: Edge-type grep over policy_parser.py: no 'PUBLIC_INBOUND'/'INTERNET_FACING' outside :245-246. Exposure goes through findings.append with id 'EC2-EXPOSURE-001' (:1483) and 'EC2-INET-001' (:1504). index.html:1226-1229 builds the CAN_ASSUME_CROSS edge with weight 4.
impact: Analysts look for exposure edges that never appear, and internet-to-instance entry points cannot be path-found from a '*'/Internet node. This is a minor documentation and UX issue with no effect on detection.
fix: Either emit `Internet -> instance` PUBLIC_INBOUND/INTERNET_FACING edges alongside the findings, which also gives Dijkstra a real entry node, or remove the weights, colours and doc rows and change attack_paths.md:80/395-396 to reference EC2-EXPOSURE-001/EC2-INET-001. Optionally list per-edge-type cross-account weights in readme.md:33.

title: Privesc findings omit the actions_any action that fired, and source_policy/resource come only from the first statement covering the first action
explanation: In _detect_privesc_paths, matched_actions is `rule.get('actions', rule.get('actions_all', []))` (:595), meaning the rule's literal list rather than what the entity holds. The actions_any member that satisfied a combo rule is never recorded. source_info comes from _find_statement_source(entity_data, trigger_action) with trigger_action = the first rule action (:579-580). That function returns the first statement whose action glob matches (:528-538). If the entity has a narrowly scoped PassRole statement before a wildcard one, the finding shows the narrow resource, which is misleading at triage.
evidence: t_perm.py. Statements are p: iam:PassRole on role/limited, p2: iam:PassRole on *, q: lambda:UpdateFunctionCode on *. Result: PRIVESC-014 matched_actions ['iam:PassRole'], source_policy 'p', resource ['arn:aws:iam::<acct>:role/limited']. lambda:UpdateFunctionCode and policy q are not mentioned, and the wildcard grant in p2 is hidden. For an entity holding only Action '*': PRIVESC-014 matched_actions ['iam:PassRole'], although the entity actually holds '*'.
impact: Analysts can't see which policy or action makes a combo path work. They may dismiss a real CRITICAL because the displayed resource looks restricted, or remediate the wrong policy. Detection itself is not affected.
fix: For each required and matched-any action, collect every effective statement that grants it. Record [{rule_action, granted_action, source, source_type, resources}], prefer and list wildcard-resource statements first, and set matched_actions to the union of the triggering rule actions, including the actions_any member that fired.

title: Cross-account detection fails for bare account-ID principals, for an unknown account_id (taken from the first role ARN), and for non-'aws' partitions in S3 ARNs
explanation: _extract_account_from_arn (:704-711) returns None for anything that isn't a colon-separated ARN, including a bare '123456789012' principal. Every analyzer takes the account it treats as 'own' from the first role ARN: :909-913 (S3), :1732-1736, :2096, :2394, :2744, :2949-2953 and :3087. When roles.json is empty or missing (for example, iam:ListRoles is denied for a low-privilege identity), account_id is None and every cross-account test evaluates false: S3 at :1034-1038 and _resource_policy_grants at :2924-2927. Bare-ID principals in S3 become same-account GRANTS_ACCESS edges. In _resource_policy_grants (ECR, DynamoDB) they produce nothing at all. _extract_bucket_from_arn only accepts the 'arn:aws:s3:::' prefix (:834), so IAM grants on arn:aws-us-gov:s3::: or arn:aws-cn:s3::: never match buckets. How often bare IDs appear in collected data depends on the service. IAM trust policies and Lambda permissions store account IDs as root ARNs, so the bare-ID case mainly affects services that keep the literal form. A service-by-service check would settle it. The caller's account is already known (main.py gets it from STS and writes it to manifest.json run_metadata.account_id), but it is not passed to analyze().
evidence: t_s3.py with account_id known: bucket statement Principal {AWS:'999999999999'} -> ('bucket:b1','999999999999','GRANTS_ACCESS'), while the root-ARN form -> GRANTS_CROSS_ACCOUNT. With roles=[] (account_id None), the root-ARN form -> GRANTS_ACCESS. _resource_policy_grants DynamoDB: bare id with account known -> edges [] findings []. Root ARN with account known -> ['DDB_GRANTS_CROSS_ACCOUNT'], ['DDB-XACCT-001']. Root ARN with account None -> [] / []. _extract_bucket_from_arn('arn:aws-us-gov:s3:::b3/*') -> (None, False), so a role with s3:GetObject on it -> no edge. Trust test: Principal {AWS:'<other-acct-id>'} -> rel is_cross_account False, findings [].
impact: External access goes unreported in some cases: bare-ID grants in services that keep them, every cross-account grant when role listing failed, and all IAM→S3 edges in GovCloud and China partitions. External accounts are mislabelled as same-account access in the graph.
fix: Pass the STS caller account into analyze(report_path, account_id=...) from main.py, or read manifest.json, and fall back to role, user or policy ARNs. Normalise principals before classifying them: a 12-digit value becomes arn:<partition>:iam::<id>:root. Make ARN parsing partition-agnostic with a regex such as ^arn:aws(-[a-z-]+)?:s3:::, and use it in _extract_bucket_from_arn and the other matchers.

title: TRUST-002 rates ExternalId-guarded and unguarded cross-account trust the same, with a fixed remediation and matched_actions, and ignores Deny
explanation: The TRUST-002 block (:774-790) fires MEDIUM for any cross-account principal and never looks at `conditions`. Its remediation always says 'add ExternalId condition', and matched_actions is hard-coded to ['sts:AssumeRole'] instead of the statement's Action, which may be AssumeRoleWithSAML, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity or TagSession. Deny statements are skipped at :730, so a cross-account Allow that an explicit Deny negates still raises TRUST-002. The NotPrincipal part of the claim does not matter for trust policies, because IAM doesn't accept NotPrincipal in role trust policies. The conditions are still recorded in trust_relationships.json, so the data is there but the finding ignores it.
evidence: t_trust.py. Cross-account root ARN with no condition -> [('TRUST-002','MEDIUM',['sts:AssumeRole'])]. Same with StringEquals sts:ExternalId -> the identical result. Action [sts:AssumeRole, sts:TagSession] -> matched_actions ['sts:AssumeRole'].
impact: Hard to prioritise. Well-guarded vendor or SaaS trusts look the same as open cross-account trusts, and the remediation text is wrong for already-guarded roles. The output is noisy but does not miss a path.
fix: Use the statement's actual Action list in matched_actions. Detect sts:ExternalId, aws:PrincipalOrgID and aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent in the conditions, rate the finding by guard strength (e.g. no guard -> MEDIUM or HIGH, ExternalId or Org -> LOW), and adjust the remediation text. Optionally subtract principals covered by explicit Deny statements in the same trust policy.

title: LOW findings (ROUTE53-DANGLING-001) are left out of the severity breakdowns in the CLI and dashboard
explanation: ROUTE53-DANGLING-001 is the only LOW finding (:3177). _generate_summary (:799-821) does count it in total_findings and in by_severity ({'LOW': n}), but has no low_count field. The CLI line at :3937 prints only CRITICAL, HIGH and MEDIUM, so LOW is visible only inside the total. The dashboard's getMaxSeverity (index.html:2008-2012) has no LOW branch, there is no .finding-badge.low rule (index.html:370-372), and the stat tiles cover critical, high, medium and total only (index.html:637-640, 2236-2240). The claim that LOW findings are invisible because of severity handling overstates the cause. The dashboard attaches findings only to user, role and group nodes (findingsMap lookups at index.html:1063, 1085, 1111). A finding with entity 'route53/<zone>' therefore never appears on any node whatever its severity, and the same is true of bucket/ and cognito/ findings.
evidence: _generate_summary([{LOW route53 finding}, {HIGH}]) -> {'total_findings': 2, 'by_severity': {'LOW': 1, 'HIGH': 1}, 'critical_count': 0, 'high_count': 1, 'medium_count': 0}. CLI format string at policy_parser.py:3937. Dashboard: getMaxSeverity returns null for LOW-only. Nodes get `findings: ef` only in the user, role and group builders.
impact: Subdomain-takeover candidates appear only in findings.json and as an unexplained difference in the total. Operators reading the CLI or dashboard won't notice them.
fix: Add low_count (and info_count) to the summary. Print LOW in the CLI line. Add a LOW branch to getMaxSeverity, a .finding-badge.low style and a stat tile. More broadly, attach non-IAM findings to their resource nodes (bucket:, route53zone:, cognito: ...) or add a findings list panel to the dashboard.

title: _is_resource_match_ec2 matches any resource containing 'ec2' and ending in '*' (wrong service, resource type, region or account)
explanation: _is_resource_match_ec2 (1232-1241) returns True for any string that contains 'ec2' (case-insensitive) and ends with '*'. It never parses the ARN. As a result: (1) non-instance EC2 ARNs such as security-group/*, volume/*, image/* and subnet/* match every instance; (2) ARNs from other services whose names contain 'ec2' match, for example arn:aws:s3:::ec2-backups/* or arn:aws:iam::*:role/ec2-*; (3) region and account are ignored, so arn:aws:ec2:<other-region>:<other-acct>:instance/* matches local instances; (4) a prefix such as instance/i-0abc* matches every instance. The substring check `instance_id in r` (1237) is harmless in practice, since only a legacy 8-hex ID can collide as a prefix. Today the `break` bug (P1-086) masks most of the fan-out, but each bogus statement still yields one fabricated edge. Once the `break` is removed, every bogus match fans out to every instance.
evidence: Repro t_ec2.py: role with ec2:TerminateInstances on arn:aws:s3:::ec2-backups/* -> ('CAN_TERMINATE','example-s3-only','..00'); role with ec2:StopInstances on arn:aws:ec2:eu-west-1:111122223333:instance/* -> CAN_MANAGE edge to a us-east-1/000000000000 instance. Direct calls: s3 arn True, iam role/ec2-* True, security-group/* True, other region/account instance/* True, instance/i-0abc* True, exact other id False.
impact: Fabricated CAN_TERMINATE/CAN_MANAGE/CAN_CONNECT edges from principals that have no effective access to the instance. Region-scoped least-privilege roles look over-privileged across all regions.
fix: Parse the resource ARN as arn:<partition>:<service>:<region>:<account>:<type>/<id>. Require service == 'ec2' and type 'instance' (or Resource '*' / 'arn:aws:ec2:*:*:*'). Match region and account against the instance: derive region from AvailabilityZone and collect OwnerId in ec2.py. Match the instance ID with fnmatchcase. For ssm:StartSession/SendCommand, consider only the instance-ARN resources in the statement.

title: SG exposure check uses exact-string CIDR equality, ignores prefix lists, and requires an IPv4 public IP
explanation: _check_sg_public_access (1244-1262) flags only literal '0.0.0.0/0' and '::/0'. Split ranges that together cover the internet (0.0.0.0/1 + 128.0.0.0/1, a known trick for evading 0.0.0.0/0 guardrails) are missed. PrefixListIds are never examined. Exposure also requires inst['PublicIpAddress'] (1460), and ec2.py collects neither Ipv6Address(es) nor per-ENI Association.PublicIp (ec2.py:29-39). So an instance that is public only over IPv6, with SG ::/0 open, can never be flagged, even though the ::/0 rule is parsed. The finding text always says '0.0.0.0/0' even when the matched rule is ::/0. The NACL/routability point is a false-positive direction rather than a false negative, and is minor. All sub-claims reproduce. Severity stays low: the common literal 0.0.0.0/0 case works.
evidence: Repro t_ec2.py: sg-0open has 22/tcp 0.0.0.0/0 and 443/tcp 0.0.0.0/1+128.0.0.0/1 -> title 'publicly exposed on 22/tcp' (443 missing). sg-split (3389 via split /1s plus a PrefixListIds rule) on an instance with a public IP -> no EXPOSURE finding. Instance with no IPv4 public IP and sg-v6 22/tcp ::/0 -> no finding.
impact: Internet exposure can be hidden from the graph by trivial CIDR splitting or customer-managed prefix lists. IPv6-only public workloads are invisible. These are false negatives for blue teams and missed entry points for red teams.
fix: Use the ipaddress module. Per rule and port range, collapse the IpRanges/Ipv6Ranges, then flag when they cover 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 (or when any prefix is shorter than about /8, as 'broad'). Collect and resolve customer-managed prefix lists (GetManagedPrefixListEntries), or flag them as 'unresolved'. In ec2.py, collect the ENI Ipv6Addresses and Association.PublicIp, and treat global IPv6 + ::/0 as exposure. Report the CIDR that actually matched in the description.

title: Main route table with an IGW default route marks every subnet in the VPC internet-routed, including subnets explicitly associated with a private route table
explanation: policy_parser.py:1326-1345 adds explicitly associated subnets of an IGW route table. When the table is Main, it then adds every subnet in the VPC (1340-1345), ignoring the fact that an explicit association to another table overrides the main table. The comment on 1339 states the correct rule ('without explicit association'), but the code does not implement it. Other confirmed details: only DestinationCidrBlock == '0.0.0.0/0' is checked, so ::/0 -> igw routes are ignored; blackhole routes are not excluded; igw_vpcs (1320-1324) is computed and never used. Severity lowered to low because EC2-INET-001 also requires a public IPv4 on an instance in an explicitly-private subnet, which is a narrow combination. The plausible case is a default VPC (main table routes to the IGW, subnets auto-assign public IPs) where someone re-associated a subnet with a private table. For the same instance, EC2-EXPOSURE-001 fires regardless of routing.
evidence: Repro t_ec2.py: rtb-main (Main, 0.0.0.0/0->igw-1); rtb-private (local only) explicitly associated with subnet-private-explicit; instance i-..01 there with a public IP -> 'EC2-INET-001 ... is internet-facing (IGW route)'. Code: `if assoc.get('Main', False): ... for sub in subnets: if sub.get('VpcId') == vpc_id: subnet_has_igw.add(sub.get('SubnetId'))`.
impact: A MEDIUM 'internet-facing' false positive for instances in explicitly private subnets. Blue teams may chase non-issues. Network-path reasoning in the graph is slightly overstated.
fix: First build explicit = {subnet_id: rtb} from non-Main associations and main_rtb = {vpc_id: rtb}. For each subnet, the effective table is explicit.get(subnet) or main_rtb[vpc]. Mark the subnet internet-routed if that table has a route to igw-* for 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 with State != 'blackhole'. Delete igw_vpcs or use it to confirm the IGW is attached.

title: EC2-IMDS-001 fires on HttpTokens=='optional' alone (terminated instances, IMDS disabled, no-role wording)
explanation: The check at 1520-1537 tests only MetadataOptions.HttpTokens == 'optional'. Confirmed false positives: (a) terminated instances, which DescribeInstances keeps returning for a while after termination and whose State is collected but ignored (ec2.py:45); (b) instances with IMDS turned off, because ec2.py:56-59 collects only HttpTokens and HttpPutResponseHopLimit, not HttpEndpoint, so HttpEndpoint='disabled' cannot be detected. The other parts are weaker. Flagging stopped instances is defensible, because the IMDSv1 setting persists and applies again on start. Instances without an instance profile still expose user-data, which often holds secrets, through IMDSv1 SSRF, so the finding is not baseless; only the 'could expose instance role credentials' wording is wrong for them. The unused hop limit does not matter for IMDSv1 risk.
evidence: Repro t_ec2.py: i-..02 (state 'stopped', no profile, optional) and i-..03 (state 'terminated', no profile, optional) -> 'EC2-IMDS-001 ... allows IMDSv1 (SSRF risk)' for both. ec2.py:56-59 MetadataOptions = {HttpTokens, HttpPutResponseHopLimit} only.
impact: Noise in MEDIUM findings: terminated or IMDS-disabled instances are reported, and the role-credential wording is misleading where no role exists. This is minor next to the true positives.
fix: In ec2.py, also collect HttpEndpoint (and optionally InstanceMetadataTags). In the parser, skip State in {'terminated', 'shutting-down'} and HttpEndpoint == 'disabled'. When there is no IamInstanceProfile, change the description to user-data/metadata exposure and consider LOW severity. Optionally lower severity for stopped instances.

title: Secret/SSM ARN matchers are case-insensitive, hardcode the 'aws' partition, match bidirectionally with '*' placeholders, and miss GetParametersByPath on a path ARN
explanation: _arn_matches_secret (1618) and _arn_matches_param (1637-1640) lowercase both sides, but secret and parameter names (the resource part of the ARN) are case-sensitive in IAM. Both require the prefix 'arn:aws:secretsmanager:' / 'arn:aws:ssm:' (1615, 1631), and the canonical parameter ARN hardcodes 'arn:aws:'. In aws-us-gov or aws-cn, scoped grants never match and only Resource '*' works; that matches the tool-wide lack of partition support (_arn_matches_lambda 2011 and _arn_matches_kms 2308 do the same). _arn_matches_param also runs fnmatch in both directions. When account_id is None (no role ARN parsed), the canonical ARN contains '*' and accepts another account's ARN for the same name. When the account is known, the reverse direction is inert, because parameter names cannot contain glob characters. GetParametersByPath on a path ARN (parameter/prod) grants reading the parameters under that path, but the matcher returns False. Every sub-claim reproduces. The false-positive cases are rare, and the path false negative is the most practical one.
evidence: Repro t_secrets.py: GovCloud resource vs GovCloud secret -> False; '...secret:PROD/*' vs 'prod/db-AbCdEf' -> True; _arn_matches_param('arn:aws:ssm:us-east-1:999999999999:parameter/prod/x','/prod/x','us-east-1',None) -> True (same with account known -> False); 'parameter/prod' vs '/prod/db/password' -> False; 'parameter/prod/*' vs same -> True; 'parameter/PROD/x' vs '/prod/x' -> True.
impact: Missing CAN_READ_PARAM edges for path-scoped SSM grants, which is a common application pattern. GovCloud and China accounts get almost no scoped secret or parameter edges. There are occasional false edges from case-folding or an unknown account.
fix: Add one shared ARN matcher. Split the ARN into fields. Treat the partition as a wildcard (or compare it to the collected ARN's partition). Compare service and region case-insensitively and the resource part with fnmatch.fnmatchcase, and match in one direction only (policy pattern against the concrete ARN). For SSM, use the parameter's collected ARN (DescribeParameters returns it) instead of building a canonical ARN with '*'. For GetParametersByPath, treat a resource equal to an ancestor path (resource + '/' is a prefix of the parameter ARN) as a match.

title: LAMBDA-URL-001 ignores the function resource policy; EBS-PUB-001 ignores account-level snapshot Block Public Access
explanation: Lambda: Step 3 (policy_parser.py:2164-2185) raises the HIGH LAMBDA-URL-001 finding whenever FunctionUrl.AuthType == 'NONE'. AuthType NONE alone does not make a URL public: the function's resource policy must also allow Principal '*' lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl, and without that statement the URL returns 403. The console adds the statement automatically, but the CLI, CloudFormation and Terraform need a separate permission. The collector stores both functions.json FunctionUrl (lambda_.py:69-76) and resource_policies/*.json (lambda_.py:93-109), and resource_policies is already loaded in the same function, so the correlation is cheap. A recent AWS change may also require lambda:InvokeFunction for new URLs; that is unverified offline. EBS: ebs.py:42-43 sets Public from createVolumePermission group 'all' only, and nothing calls GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState. In 'block-all-sharing' mode, existing public snapshots are treated as private, but the attribute persists (disabling BPA re-exposes them), so EBS-PUB-001 (policy_parser.py:3121-3129) would fire falsely. The EBS half rests on documented AWS behaviour and was not reproduced live. Both are narrow false positives.
evidence: Repro (agents/engine-d/t_url.py): function with FunctionUrl AuthType NONE and no resource-policy file -> findings ['LAMBDA-URL-001']. With the standard '*' InvokeFunctionUrl statement (Condition lambda:FunctionUrlAuthType=NONE) -> ['LAMBDA-URL-001'] and LAMBDA_GRANTS_PUBLIC has_conditions=True (LAMBDA-PUB-001 correctly suppressed). grep for block_public_access/get_snapshot_block -> no matches in app/.
impact: An occasional false HIGH 'publicly invocable' finding for URLs that actually return 403, and false HIGH 'public snapshot' findings in accounts that use EBS snapshot BPA block-all-sharing. This is minor noise for blue teams, and red teams may waste a request.
fix: Lambda: in Step 3, look up resource_policies.get(fn_arn) and require an Allow statement with Principal '*' or {'AWS':'*'} whose actions cover lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl (or lambda:*/*). Otherwise downgrade to INFO ('AuthType NONE but not publicly authorised'). EBS: in ebs.py, call ec2.get_snapshot_block_public_access_state() once per region and store the State. In the parser, suppress or downgrade EBS-PUB-001 when State == 'block-all-sharing'; 'block-new-sharing' leaves existing public snapshots exposed.

title: Multi-region KMS key replicas share one key policy in the analyzer (key_policies keyed by KeyId)
explanation: _load_kms_data stores key_policies[kp['KeyId']] (policy_parser.py:2365), and Step 2 looks policies up by key['KeyId'] (:2450). Multi-region replicas share the 'mrk-...' KeyId but have independent per-region key policies. When the sibling-region scan loads more than one region, the last region read (os.listdir order) overwrites the others, and every replica is evaluated against that one policy. The collector writes a per-region file that already contains the regional Arn (kms.py:90-91), so the data needed for a correct key is on disk. The bug is currently latent: in --all mode, analyze(global_path) runs at main.py:149, before any region is enumerated. It surfaces on a re-analysis, when an earlier same-day --all run left region dirs behind, and as soon as the known ordering bug is fixed. Single-region mode always has its own kms/ dir, so it is not affected.
evidence: Repro (agents/engine-d/t_kms.py): same mrk KeyId in us-east-1 (policy: Principal '*' Decrypt) and eu-west-1 (policy: cross-account root only), analyze from <tmp>/global -> findings [('KMS-PUB-001','eu-west-1'), ('KMS-PUB-001','us-east-1')]; no KMS-XACCT-001 for eu-west-1. The eu-west-1 replica is falsely reported public, and its real cross-account grant is lost.
impact: In multi-region analysis, KMS-PUB and KMS-XACCT findings and key-policy edges can be attributed to the wrong replica: false public-key alerts on one replica and missed cross-account grants on another. This only matters for accounts that use MRKs whose replica policies differ.
fix: Key the policy map by ARN: key_policies[kp.get('Arn') or kp['KeyId']] = kp, and look it up with key_policies.get(key.get('Arn')) or key_policies.get(key.get('KeyId')). Also fix the --all ordering (main.py:149) so this path is actually exercised and tested.

title: API Gateway INVOKES targets keep alias qualifiers and ${stageVariables} so they don't join the real Lambda node
explanation: Confirmed. `_extract_lambda_arn` (app/components/apigateway.py:17-25) cuts the URI at '/invocations' and keeps a `:qualifier` suffix and `${stageVariables.x}` placeholders. INVOKES targets `lambda:{fn}` (:3025-3027), while Lambda nodes are `lambda:{unqualified FunctionArn}` (:2139, :2156). The edge is not quite dangling: the dashboard creates a separate placeholder lambda node labelled with the qualifier (index.html:1855-1867). That placeholder is disconnected from the real function's USES_ROLE edge, so the API → Lambda → execution-role path is broken.
evidence:
t2_extra.py:
  _extract_lambda_arn(alias URI)    -> arn:aws:lambda:eu-west-2:<acct>:function:fn:live
  _extract_lambda_arn(stagevar URI) -> arn:aws:lambda:eu-west-2:<acct>:function:${stageVariables.fn}
  INVOKES target 'lambda:...function:fn:live'; lambda analyzer node 'lambda:...function:fn'; joins? False
impact: Internet → API → Lambda → role attack paths are cut whenever APIs integrate through aliases or stage variables, which is common in staged deployments.
fix: In the collector or analyzer, normalise to the unqualified function ARN (strip the 8th ':' segment) and keep the qualifier as an edge attribute. For ${stageVariables.*}, resolve the value from get_stages()[].variables (REST) or get_stages (v2); if it cannot be resolved, emit the edge with an 'unresolved' flag and no target node.

title: Exposure findings and edges ignore internal/private signals (ELB scheme, private zones, internal K8s LBs, IAM-auth/private APIs, Function URL policy)
explanation: Each sub-item checks out. (a) EXPOSES edges are emitted for every ELB target regardless of Scheme (:3160-3172; only ELB-PUB-001 is gated at :3150), even though docs/attack_paths.md:259 ties EXPOSES to internet-facing LBs. (b) ROUTE53-DANGLING-001 (:3175-3184) ignores the collected `Private` flag (route53.py:71). (c) K8S-NET-001 (:3659-3675) flags every LoadBalancer service as HIGH 'public exposure' without checking the aws-load-balancer-internal or aws-load-balancer-scheme annotations; the AWS LB Controller defaults to an internal scheme. (d) APIGW-AUTH-001 (:3028) uses only `HasAuthorizer`, which is the count of authorizer resources (apigateway.py:51-55, :86-90). AWS_IAM method/route auth creates no authorizer resource, and PRIVATE endpoint type is never collected, so both are reported unauthenticated. There is also an unreported false negative: one authorizer on an API hides other methods that use NONE. (e) LAMBDA-URL-001 (:2165-2183) checks only AuthType, not whether the resource policy allows Principal '*' lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl; the console adds that permission automatically, so false positives are rare.
evidence:
t2_extra.py: internal LB -> edges [('EXPOSES','internal')]; private zone with candidate -> ('ROUTE53-DANGLING-001','LOW'); API with HasAuthorizer False (the AWS_IAM case) -> ('APIGW-AUTH-001','MEDIUM').
t3_k8s.py: Service annotated aws-load-balancer-internal=true -> 'K8S-NET-001 HIGH Service apps/svc-int is LoadBalancer (public exposure)'.
impact: False-positive exposure findings and edges, mostly LOW/MEDIUM, though K8S-NET-001 is HIGH. They add noise to external-attack-surface triage and draw internet-exposure paths that do not exist.
fix: ELB: emit EXPOSES only for internet-facing LBs, or use a separate FRONTS edge for internal ones. Route53: skip or downgrade candidates in Private zones. K8S-NET-001: read the service annotations (aws-load-balancer-internal, aws-load-balancer-scheme), loadBalancerSourceRanges and status.load_balancer.ingress hostname ('internal-' prefix). APIGW: collect per-method authorizationType (REST get_method) and per-route authorizationType (HTTP get_routes) plus endpointConfiguration.types, skip PRIVATE, and flag only NONE methods/routes. LAMBDA-URL-001: confirm a public InvokeFunctionUrl statement exists in the resource policy.

title: policy_parser.py maintainability: duplicated loaders/walkers/stanzas, 456-line K8s function, dead code, no tests
explanation: The measurements are accurate. AST lengths: _analyze_k8s_relationships 3294-3749 (456 lines), _analyze_secrets_relationships 1722-1966 (245), analyze 3796-3982 (187), plus S3 241 and EC2 280. There are 9 `_load_region`/fallback loaders with three or four different fallback rules: 'local dir exists else siblings', 'always local + siblings when basename == global' (extra, :3063-3075), and 'siblings when no clusters' (k8s, :3266). The account_id loop appears 7 times. Dead code: known_arns at :1739-1745 is never read (S3's at :1046 is effectively a no-op, `pval if pval in known_arns else pval`), role_by_name at :3305, sec_ctx at :3456, and KMS_GRANTS_DECRYPT exists only in the weights dict (:2296). There are no test files outside .venv, reports and tmp. The duplication directly produced several verified bugs in this batch (P1-115 repeated in seven places, P1-114 in seven, the inconsistent K8s fallback in P1-043/125).
evidence: AST scan: _analyze_k8s_relationships 3294 3749 456; _analyze_secrets_relationships 1722 1966 245; analyze 3796 3982 187. grep -c "account_id = _extract_account_from_arn(r.get('Arn', ''))" -> 7. find (excluding .venv/reports/tmp) -name '*test*' -> nothing.
impact: Fixes must be applied in five to seven places, and they drift: the same bug class recurs across analyzers. Without tests, regressions such as the --all ordering bug go unnoticed.
fix: Extract shared helpers: `_region_paths(report_path, svc_dirs)` with a single explicit --all rule, `_account_id(roles)`, `_iter_statements`, and one resource-policy evaluator used by S3/secrets/lambda/kms/messaging/newsurface. Make analyze() table-driven with per-analyzer try/except. Split the K8s analyzer into per-concern functions. Delete the dead code. Add pytest with synthetic report fixtures, starting with the repros from this verification.

title: K8S-IRSA-ADMIN looks up the IRSA role by name only, so a cross-account role with the same name as a local admin role triggers CRITICAL
explanation: Confirmed for the cross-account case. `role_name_from_arn = irsa_arn.split('/')[-1]` is looked up in permission_map['roles'] by name (:3368-3370), ignoring the account ID. The edge itself records iam_role_known=False (:3363), but the finding uses the local role's permissions anyway. The dashboard makes this worse: it resolves IAM ARN targets by name via findNodeId (index.html:1400-1404, :1993-2004), so the SA is drawn pointing at the local admin role node. The 'path role' part of the claim does not hold: RoleName is the last path segment and is unique per account, so for same-account path roles the name lookup is correct. Severity is lowered because the scenario needs cross-account IRSA, an identical role name, and admin rights on the local role, which is uncommon in combination. Shared role names such as controller roles do occur in multi-account estates.
evidence:
t3_k8s.py: SA apps/ext annotated with arn:aws:iam::<other-acct>:role/app-admin; local role 'app-admin' has '*' on '*' ->
  edge iam_role_known=False, yet finding 'K8S-IRSA-ADMIN CRITICAL ServiceAccount apps/ext (cluster c1) has IRSA -> admin IAM role'.
node t5_xss.js: the other-account ARN resolves to the local role node arn:aws:iam::<acct>:role/app-admin.
impact: A CRITICAL false positive and a fabricated SA-to-admin-role path in the graph, pointing at the wrong account's role.
fix: Engine: build an ARN-to-RoleName map from roles.json and run the admin check only when irsa_arn exactly matches a known role ARN. Otherwise mark the role external/unknown and skip the permission check, or emit INFO. Dashboard: resolve IAM ARNs by exact ARN first and fall back to a name match only when the account ID matches. Fixing P1-117 by full-ARN lookup also covers this.

title: Finding noise: per-pod K8S-DEFAULT-SA, built-in cluster-admin flagged, over-broad PARAM-PLAIN-001 name patterns, per-statement IAM edges
explanation: All four sources of noise are real. (1) K8S-DEFAULT-SA is emitted per pod (:3437-3452), so every ReplicaSet replica repeats it, and automount_service_account_token is not considered. (2) K8S-RBAC-002 (:3618-3644) fires on the built-in cluster-admin ClusterRole present in every cluster. (3) SENSITIVE_PARAM_PATTERNS (:1597-1601) uses unanchored substrings ('*cred*', '*token*', '*secret*'), which match credit_limit, accredited, tokenizer, max_tokens and secretary_name. (4) The IAM → resource loops emit one edge per matching effective statement (for example S3 Step 1 :917-962), so console edge counts are inflated. The dashboard de-duplicates by edge id, so the graph itself is fine.
evidence:
_looks_sensitive_param_name: '/app/credit_limit' True, '/app/tokenizer/model' True, '/svc/accredited' True, '/x/max_tokens' True, '/app/secretary_name' True.
t3_k8s.py: 'K8S-RBAC-002 HIGH Role cluster/cluster-admin has * on *'; K8S-DEFAULT-SA emitted for each pod, including one with automount_service_account_token False.
impact: Alert fatigue: real findings are buried under repeated MEDIUM default-SA entries and HIGH built-in-role entries, and false credential-in-plaintext hits. Edge counts overstate coverage.
fix: Aggregate K8S-DEFAULT-SA by owner (metadata.owner_references, i.e. ReplicaSet/Deployment) or by namespace, and skip it when automount is disabled on the pod or SA. Exclude built-in roles (cluster-admin, system:*) from K8S-RBAC-002 and report only their non-system bindings. Use token-boundary regexes such as `(^|[/_.-])(password|passwd|secret|token|api[-_]?key|credentials?|private[-_]key)($|[/_.-])`. De-duplicate IAM edges per (source, target, type) and merge source_policy lists.

title: K8s SELECTS edge construction is O(services × pods-in-namespace × total pods)
explanation: The complexity defect is real. For each service, the loop at :3677-3696 walks pod_lookup and, for each pod in the same namespace, rescans `cdata['pods']` from the start to find that pod's labels. The reviewer's cubic extrapolation (about 9 min for 3,000 pods / 300 services) assumes every pod is in one namespace. The `p_ns != ns` filter cuts the cost to S × P_ns × P. With pods spread over 30 namespaces, 3,000 pods / 300 services takes about 9 s, not 9 min. Large single-namespace clusters can still take minutes, but the typical cost is seconds.
evidence:
t3_k8s.py (single namespace): 200/20 -> 0.15s; 400/40 -> 1.25s; 800/80 -> 9.91s (about x8 per doubling, as claimed).
t4_perf.py: pods=3000 namespaces=30 services=300 -> 8.8s.
impact: Slower analysis on large or monolithic-namespace clusters, minutes in the worst case. It does not block analysis or affect results.
fix: Before the services loop, build `pods_by_ns = defaultdict(list)` of (pod_id, labels) once per cluster, then for each service iterate only `pods_by_ns[ns]`. This is O(S × P_ns) with no rescans. A ~10-line change.

title: Doc/label drift: output file list, missing ELB doc anchor, SECRET-XAUTH naming & ExternalId remediation, KMS_GRANTS_DECRYPT, ClusterRole labelled 'Role', LOW count omitted
explanation: Mostly right, with some miscounts. The module docstring (:4-15) lists 5 outputs, but readme.md:154-156 lists 7, not 5. The code writes 14 files (13 relationship/analysis files plus summary.json, :3887-3931), not 13. _DOC_ANCHORS (:3761-3781) has no 'ELB' key, so ELB-PUB-001 links to the bare doc. SECRET-XAUTH-001 (:1925) breaks the *-XACCT-001 convention. Its remediation 'consider adding ExternalId' (:1937-1938) is wrong because sts:ExternalId exists only on AssumeRole requests and would deny every GetSecretValue. docs/attack_paths.md:402 documents KMS_GRANTS_DECRYPT, which is never emitted. K8S-RBAC-002 derives kind from `role.get('kind')` (:3621), which is None for list items returned by the K8s API, so ClusterRoles are labelled 'Role'. summary.json does include LOW inside `by_severity`, but there is no `low_count`, and the console line (:3934-3940) and dashboard tiles show only critical/high/medium.
evidence: t3_k8s.py: 'K8S-RBAC-002 HIGH Role cluster/cluster-admin has * on *'. _doc_reference('ELB-PUB-001') -> DOC_BASE + '' (no 'ELB' key). Control analyze() run wrote 14 files. readme.md:154-156 lists findings, permission_map, trust_relationships, s3, ec2, k8s, summary (7).
impact: Misleading docs and labels. The SECRET-XAUTH remediation would break legitimate access if followed, ELB findings lose their attack-path link, and LOW findings are invisible in the run summary.
fix: Update the docstring and readme to list all 14 outputs. Add 'ELB' to _DOC_ANCHORS. Rename SECRET-XAUTH-001 to SECRET-XACCT-001 (keep the old id as an alias for one release) and change the remediation to 'scope Principal to specific role ARNs or add aws:PrincipalOrgID'. Remove KMS_GRANTS_DECRYPT from the docs and the weights dict, or implement it. Set r_kind by source list (roles vs cluster_roles), not role['kind']. Add low_count to summary.json and LOW to the console line and dashboard tiles.

title: Dashboard loads JSZip and Cytoscape from cdnjs at runtime with no SRI/CSP and nothing vendored, so it has a CDN trust dependency, does not work offline and makes a third-party request
explanation: Lines 7-8 are plain `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/...">` tags with no integrity or crossorigin attributes. The file has no CSP meta tag (grep for integrity/Content-Security-Policy/http-equiv returns nothing). serve_dashboard uses a bare SimpleHTTPRequestHandler (app/utils/dashboard.py:39), so no CSP header is sent either. The page then holds the whole client report in `reportData`. A tampered response from the CDN or a TLS-intercepting proxy would run with full access to that data and unrestricted connect-src. pyproject.toml package-data ships only index.html and icons/*.svg (line 40), so the libraries are never vendored. Offline, both scripts fail. Because JSZip is referenced inside the try block, the user sees 'Error loading zip: JSZip is not defined' (index.html:934-936), not a hang. The opsec leak is real but small: each load reveals the operator's IP and timing to cdnjs, plus an origin-only Referer of http://127.0.0.1:<port>/. No doc explicitly promises offline use; README only says 'no AWS credentials needed'. The versioned cdnjs paths are effectively immutable, so the realistic risk is low. P1-185's secondary claims also hold: Dockerfile:1 `python:3.13-slim` (tag, not digest), requirements.txt and pyproject list unpinned `boto3`/`kubernetes`, and docker-publish.yml uses `actions/checkout@v4`, `docker/login-action@v3`, `setup-buildx-action@v3`, `build-push-action@v6` (mutable tags).
evidence: index.html:7 `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/jszip/3.10.1/jszip.min.js"></script>`, :8 cytoscape 3.30.4 the same; `grep -n 'integrity\|Content-Security\|crossorigin\|http-equiv' index.html` returns no output; pyproject.toml:40 `"app" = ["dashboard/index.html", "dashboard/icons/*.svg"]`. Harness with JSZip and cytoscape undefined: `overlay text: "Error loading zip: JSZip is not defined"`, caught, no hang. Dockerfile:1, requirements.txt (2 unpinned lines), .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:22,37,43,46.
impact: A CDN or proxy compromise could exfiltrate a client's full IAM, trust and findings graph from the analyst's browser. The dashboard cannot be used on air-gapped or egress-restricted analysis hosts, which are typical for sensitive engagement data. Each use makes a small third-party network request.
fix: Vendor jszip.min.js and cytoscape.min.js into app/dashboard/vendor/, add them to package-data, and reference them by relative path. Add a restrictive CSP meta tag, for example `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'none'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`. If the CDN is kept, add `integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous"`. Optionally set the same CSP as a response header in serve_dashboard. For P1-185's build inputs, pin the base image by digest, pin deps with a lock file or hashes, and pin Actions to commit SHAs.

title: No node filter for 17 emitted node types, many missing from the legend, 7 edge categories without a checkbox, and a dead 'finding' edge filter and style
explanation: Node filter checkboxes (646-662) cover only user, role, group, policy, instance, bucket, sg, cluster, pod, sa, k8srole, k8ssecret, k8sservice, k8singress, secret and ssmparam. The dashboard also creates kms, lambda, sqs and sns (S3 section 1278-1283), nodegroup (K8s prefixes, 1414), ecstask, cfnstack, gluejob, codebuild and sagemaker (COMPUTE_PREFIXES 1702), ecr, rds, apigw and dynamodb (NEWSURFACE_PREFIXES 1838), and cognito, ebssnapshot and elb (EXTRA_PREFIXES 1906). That is exactly 17 types with no filter. The legend (734-753) lacks 15 of them: k8sservice, k8singress, nodegroup, the 5 compute types, ecr, rds, apigw, dynamodb, cognito, ebssnapshot and elb. Edge filters (668-684) have no entry for the analyzer categories messaging (policy_parser.py:2789/2816/2841), ecr and dynamodb (prefix at 2911/2929, dynamodb at 2989), apigw (3027), cognito (3101/3104), ebs (3123/3134) or elb (3171), nor for the fallbacks 'newsurface' and 'extra'. applyFilters (2345-2375) hides only when `filters[x] === false`, so these always show and cannot be toggled. Nothing creates category 'finding' in either the dashboard or the analyzer, so the 'Findings (privesc, danger)' checkbox (670) and the `edge[category="finding"]` style (2121) are dead. This is a usability problem only; graph data is not lost.
evidence: grep `"finding"|'finding'` matches only index.html:670 and :2121. Prefix arrays: index.html:1414 validK8sPrefixes, 1702, 1770, 1838, 1906. Analyzer edge categories confirmed by grep of `"category"` in policy_parser.py (2789, 2911, 2929, 2989, 3027, 3101, 3104, 3123, 3134, 3171).
impact: Analysts cannot declutter large graphs by hiding compute, data-store or messaging nodes or the newer edge classes. Users may assume the 'Findings' toggle hides privesc edges when it does nothing, and the legend cannot identify many node shapes and colours.
fix: Generate the node-filter checkboxes and legend from NODE_COLORS/NODE_SHAPES (one source of truth). Add edge-filter entries for messaging, ecr, dynamodb, apigw, cognito, ebs, elb, newsurface and extra, or generate them from the categories actually present in the loaded graph. Remove the 'finding' checkbox and style, or create real finding edges, for example privesc edges from the analyzer.

title: Zip loading has no size or entry limits and inflates every *.json, including files the dashboard never reads (permission_map.json is parsed and kept but unused)
explanation: The mechanics are as described. loadZipFile (917-937) runs `JSZip.loadAsync(file)` and then inflates every non-directory entry ending in .json to a string in parallel, with no checks on compressed or uncompressed size or entry count. That includes iam/policy_documents/*, inline policy dumps, VPC/WAF/CloudTrail data and K8s dumps that processLoadedFiles never reads. reportData.permissionMap is parsed at 1004 and never referenced again (grep finds only that line), so it stays in memory for the page's lifetime. The threat is weaker than claimed. The operator chooses the zip, normally their own tool output, so the 'crafted zip bomb' case needs an attacker-supplied report and only crashes the operator's own tab. A single entry over V8's ~512M-char string limit throws RangeError, which the try/catch here does catch. The `files` strings are transient and can be garbage-collected after buildGraph, so the extra memory is mainly a peak cost, plus the retained permissionMap. The '2-3x' figure was not measured.
evidence: index.html:920-932 `const zip = await JSZip.loadAsync(file); ... zip.forEach((relPath, zipEntry) => { if (!zipEntry.dir && relPath.endsWith('.json')) { promises.push(zipEntry.async('string')...` with no size checks; index.html:1004 `reportData.permissionMap = readJSON(...'analysis/permission_map.json') || {};` is the only reference; iam.py:257/304/335/358/381 write per-policy and inline JSON that the dashboard does not read.
impact: Very large accounts or K8s-heavy reports use more browser memory and load more slowly than needed, which could crash the tab on low-memory analyst machines. A malicious shared report could crash the tab; there is no confidentiality or integrity impact.
fix: Inflate only the whitelist of paths readJSON needs (the iam/*.json files, analysis/*.json except permission_map.json, s3/buckets.json and */ec2/instances.json). Skip entries whose `zipEntry._data.uncompressedSize` exceeds a cap such as 200 MB, cap the total, and show a clear error. Remove the unused permissionMap load.

title: processLoadedFiles is not awaited, so every graph-build exception escapes the try/catch and the UI hangs silently
explanation: loadZipFile calls `processLoadedFiles(files);` at 933 without await. processLoadedFiles is declared `async` (940), so any throw in it, in buildGraph, initGraph, updateStats or populatePathSelectors becomes a rejected promise that nothing handles. The catch at 934-936 never runs, the overlay text stays 'Loading...' and the overlay is never hidden (the hide happens at 1977, after initGraph). One nuance: in the fully offline case JSZip is also missing and fails inside the try, so that case is reported properly. A Cytoscape-only failure (partial CDN block, script blocker) or any data-shape error is silent. This defect is what turns P1-146 into an unexplained hang.
evidence: index.html:933 `processLoadedFiles(files);` inside `try {...} catch (err) { overlay.querySelector('.drop-text').textContent = 'Error loading zip: ' + err.message; }` (934-936); 940 `async function processLoadedFiles(files) {`. Harness with JSZip present and cytoscape undefined: `overlay text: "Loading..." | overlay hidden: false | cy built: false`, `unhandledRejection: ["cytoscape is not defined"]`, console: [] (the catch never ran).
impact: Any malformed or unexpected report data, or a library load failure, leaves the analyst on an endless 'Loading...' screen with no error message. Diagnosis requires DevTools, and real data problems such as P1-146 are hidden.
fix: Use `await processLoadedFiles(files);`, or make it a plain synchronous function since it contains no await. Wrap buildGraph in try/catch so the overlay shows 'Error building graph: <msg>' and the stack is logged. Add a `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', ...)` fallback that surfaces errors in the overlay.

title: readJSON returns the first suffix match in iteration order, not the file under the detected root, which can silently mix runs when a zip holds more than one
explanation: readJSON (973-988) tests `path === fullPath || path.endsWith('/' + relPath) || path === relPath` in one pass over Object.entries(files) and returns the first hit. The exact `rootPrefix + relPath` match is not preferred. rootPrefix comes from the first manifest.json in iteration order (944-949). `files` is filled in promise-resolution order of zipEntry.async(), which need not match zip order. So when a zip contains more than one run, users, roles, findings and instances can come from a different run than the manifest and from each other, with no warning. The trigger is narrower than it sounds: the tool's own `--zip` (main.py:252-255, 278-281) archives exactly one run, either the account dir for --all or one region dir. The bug affects hand-built zips, for example zipping reports/<date>/ or an account folder that holds several single-region runs. In that case per-region data such as ec2/instances.json and analysis/* may come from the wrong region.
evidence: index.html:976 `if (path === fullPath || path.endsWith('/' + relPath) || path === relPath) {`. Harness, zip with acctA/us-east-1/manifest.json first and acctB/eu-west-2/iam/users.json earlier in iteration than acctA's users.json: `users loaded: ["user-from-B"]` while the root is from acctA, with no error shown.
impact: An analyst who loads a combined zip can get an attack graph mixing identities, findings and instances from different accounts or regions. That is silent data corruption of the graph, but it only happens for user-assembled multi-run archives.
fix: In readJSON, first look up `files[rootPrefix + relPath]` exactly, and fall back to suffix matching only under rootPrefix (`path.startsWith(rootPrefix)`). Detect more than one manifest.json and either warn or let the user pick the run.

title: Copy-pasted edge-family loops, dead code, and reload/persistence gaps in the dashboard
explanation: Most sub-claims were verified. The reviewer counted nine loops; there are ten nearly identical edge-family loops (S3, EC2, K8s, Secrets, Lambda, KMS, Compute, Messaging, Newsurface, Extra) spanning index.html:1254-1971. This duplication is the root cause of the inconsistencies found elsewhere: S3 uses `weight || 1` and has no dedupe, cross-account handling differs by family, and non-S3 families leave orphan placeholders. The S3 loop pushes edges without an `elements.some` check (:1305-1319), so duplicate IDs reach Cytoscape. A realistic trigger is a bucket policy with two Allow statements for the same principal. Cytoscape 3.x skips duplicate IDs at creation, so the effect is only lost metadata (e.g. the second statement's granted_actions), not a crash. Dead or unused code confirmed: NODE_SHAPES (:790) is never referenced, and node shape is hardcoded 'ellipse'. reportData.securityGroups (:1345, :1354) is never assigned, so SG nodes always show the raw sg- ID. reportData.permissionMap (:1004) and reportData.manifest (:1016) are loaded but never read. The `seen` dedupe in findAllAttackPaths (:2811-2820) is a no-op, because each (source, target) pair is pushed at most once. The 'global/iam/users.json' branch (:960-964) is unreachable, because the preceding `includes('iam/users.json')` always matches first; it only matters for zips without manifest.json, and main.py always writes one (main.py:85). The findAllAttackPaths reassignment wrapper (:2989-2998) works but is fragile. No localStorage, export or download code exists, so owned marks and paths are lost on reload. Account, region and date are never displayed, although manifest.json carries run_metadata.account_id/region/timestamps (main.py:67-82). Loading a second report through the always-visible 'Load Report' button (:596) or by dropping a file on the body keeps the old state: buildGraph() never resets it, and only clearGraph() does (:2716-2748).
evidence: Harness s3_misc.js (same dir): 'duplicate ids passed to cytoscape: [bucket:b->arn:aws:iam::<A>:role/x:GRANTS_ACCESS]' (the same pair via KMS was deduped). After a second processLoadedFiles: owned=[alice ARN], focused=alice ARN, discoveredPaths=1, attack-paths-list HTML unchanged, owned-list still lists alice, focus-bar still active. highlightDiscoveredPath(0) then operates on elements of the destroyed Cytoscape instance. `grep -n NODE_SHAPES` returns only the definition at :790; `grep localStorage|download|export` returns nothing.
impact: Mostly maintainability. Each copy-pasted loop has drifted, and those drifts cause real accuracy bugs (weight coercion, cross-account handling). For operators: stale attack paths and owned marks from a previous report stay on screen after loading a new one, which can be mistaken for results of the new account. Engagement state (owned nodes, discovered paths) cannot be saved or exported. Nothing shows which account, region or date is loaded, which matters when switching between several client reports.
fix: Replace the ten loops with one table-driven `addFamilyEdges(edges, {prefixes, colors, defaultCategory})` that shares the resolver, placeholder creation, Set-based dedupe and `weight ?? 1`. Delete NODE_SHAPES or apply it in the style. Populate securityGroups from ec2 data or drop the lookup. Remove the no-op dedupe, the unreachable branch and the wrapper (fold the playback logic into findAllAttackPaths). Call a resetState() (the non-DOM part of clearGraph) at the start of processLoadedFiles. Show manifest.run_metadata (account, region(s), timestamp) in the header. Add JSON export/import of owned nodes and discovered paths, with localStorage keyed by account and timestamp.

title: Falsy-zero in path-selector sort puts users after other types
explanation: populatePathSelectors sorts with `const ta = typeOrder[a.data('type')] || 99;` (index.html:2254-2255), and typeOrder.user is 0 (:2253). `0 || 99` is 99, so users fall into the 'other' bucket: after roles, instances, groups, buckets and policies, and interleaved alphabetically with kms/lambda/pod and similar nodes. This is the same `|| default` falsy-zero pattern as the weight bug.
evidence: index.html:2253-2255. Harness s3_misc.js path-from order: ['[role] m-role', '[bucket] b-bucket', '[user] aa-user', '[kms] k1', '[user] zz-user'].
impact: Cosmetic and UX only. Users, the most common 'compromised source', are buried in long dropdowns on large accounts. Path results are unaffected.
fix: Use `typeOrder[type] ?? 99`, or index from 1.

title: Node/edge filters are display-only; path finding traverses and highlights hidden elements
explanation: applyFilters (index.html:2347-2375) only toggles the 'hidden-filter' class, whose style is `display: none` (:2172-2175). findPath (:2286) and findAllAttackPaths (:2783) both run Dijkstra on `cy.elements()`, which includes hidden elements.
