The returned path can therefore run through nodes and edges the user filtered out. These are highlighted while still invisible, and the step list names hops the user cannot see. Filtering only the display is a legitimate design choice, so this is a UX/expectation issue: users cannot exclude an edge category (e.g. 'k8s_structural' or 'kms') from analysis. Since categories are the natural way to drop non-traversable edges, this partly overlaps the undirected-traversal fix.
evidence: index.html:2358-2374 add/remove 'hidden-filter'; :2286 and :2783 `cy.elements().dijkstra(...)`. Harness s3_misc.js: with every edge given 'hidden-filter', findPath still returns cost 2.0 and highlights 'CAN_ASSUME(hidden)'.
impact: Confusing results: highlighted paths have invisible hops, and an operator who hides an edge class they consider noise still gets paths through it. This is a minor accuracy and trust issue, not a security one.
fix: Run Dijkstra on `cy.elements().not('.hidden-filter')`, or `cy.elements(':visible')`, behind a 'Respect filters in path finding' checkbox that defaults to on. Rerun or clear the displayed path when filters change.

title: Finding id/title/severity/reference rendered unescaped and href has no scheme allow-list (exploitable only with a tampered report)
explanation: The code matches the description. f.severity goes into a class attribute (:2518-2519), f.id and f.title go into innerHTML (:2523), and f.reference goes into `<a href="...">` without escaping or a scheme check (:2525). Exploitation needs a modified report, though. In reports the tool generates, f.reference is always the constant GitHub URL from _doc_reference (policy_parser.py:3756/3784-3789, set at :3885). f.id and f.severity are constants. Only findings whose entity is user/, role/ or group/ are attached to nodes (index.html:1061-1110), and their titles are built from constants or a validated account ID (policy_parser.py:586, 668, 762, 780). So no value an attacker can plant in the target account reaches this sink. Anyone who can tamper with the zip can already inject through any label or ARN (merged XSS issue), so this sink adds a defence-in-depth gap rather than a new attack path.
evidence: index.html:2519 `html += `${f.id} ${f.severity} `;` ; :2523 `html += `${f.id}: ${f.title}`;` ; :2525 `html += ` `. Harness (test_misc.js) with a hand-edited finding: `title raw: true`, `href` carried a `javascript:` URL through unchanged (payload elided). policy_parser.py:3787-3789 always returns `f"{DOC_BASE}{_DOC_ANCHORS.get(prefix, '')}"`.
impact: An analyst who opens a report zip from an untrusted party (the tool advertises zips 'for easy transport') can get script execution when they click an IAM node that has findings. Freshly generated reports are not affected.
fix: Escape f.id, f.title and f.severity with the shared esc() helper. Allow-list the class (`['critical','high','medium','low','info'].includes(cls) ? cls : 'info'`). Accept f.reference only when `new URL(f.reference).protocol === 'https:'` (optionally only github.com), and otherwise leave out the link.

title: Clear button throws TypeError in updateStats() and skips the rest of the reset, leaking the playback timer
explanation: clearGraph sets `reportData = {}` (:2719) and then calls updateStats() (:2731), which reads `reportData.users.length` (:2229) and throws. Everything after that line is skipped: graph-info, path-result, attack-paths list and status, playback controls, stopPlayback() (:2738), _discoveredPaths and the '-' stat reset. The overlay and owned list are reset because that happens before the throw. The reviewer's note about the playback timer understates the effect. If playback was running when Clear was pressed, the interval keeps firing. Once a new report is loaded, highlightDiscoveredPath (:2859-2866) calls `cy.elements().addClass('dimmed')` on the new graph every tick, using stale path collections from the destroyed instance. The Play button also stays on 'Stop'. A page reload or pressing Stop recovers.
evidence: index.html:2719 `reportData = {};` ; :2731 `updateStats();` ; :2229 `document.getElementById('stat-users').textContent = reportData.users.length;`. Harness (test_misc.js): `clearGraph: THREW Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length') | list len before/after 449 449 | playback timer still running true | _discoveredPaths 1 | status "1 paths found ..."`. test_clear.js (load a new report after Clear while playback was running): `btn-play text: Stop`, `new graph nodes dimmed by leaked playback timer: 2/2 | stale list still present: true`.
impact: After Clear, stale attack paths, stats and status stay on screen, and an uncaught TypeError appears in the console. If playback was active, the next report's graph keeps getting dimmed until the operator presses Stop or reloads. This is cosmetic and a reliability nuisance; no data is wrong.
fix: In clearGraph, call stopPlayback() first and remove the updateStats() call, since the explicit '-' reset at :2741-2745 already covers it. Alternatively, make updateStats defensive (`(reportData.users || []).length`, etc.). Also reset path selectors, _currentPathIdx and the attack-path list before destroying cy.

title: API Gateway Lambda-target extraction keeps alias/version qualifiers and stage-variable placeholders, and only recognises the aws partition
explanation: _extract_lambda_arn (apigateway.py:17-25) slices from 'arn:aws:lambda:' to '/invocations' and does nothing else. (1) An alias- or version-qualified integration ('...function:fn:prod/invocations') gives a qualified ARN. The parser emits INVOKES to 'lambda:<qualified>' (policy_parser.py:3025-3027). The Lambda node the rest of the graph uses is 'lambda:<unqualified FunctionArn>' (policy_parser.py:2139/2156), so the dashboard's newsurface loop (index.html:1855-1870) creates a separate orphan placeholder labelled 'prod'. The apigw -> lambda -> USES_ROLE -> role chain is therefore broken. (2) Stage-variable URIs ('function:${stageVariables.fn}') produce a literal placeholder node in the same way. (3) URIs in the aws-us-gov or aws-cn partitions return None, and the API ARNs at :60 and :94 hard-code 'arn:aws:'. However, the whole tool assumes the aws partition (for example, the dashboard tests startsWith('arn:aws:iam:')), so this part is systemic, not specific to this function. (4) Ignoring HTTP/VPC-link integrations is the documented scope of the module ('Lambda integration targets' in the docstring), so it is a coverage limitation, not a bug. APIGW-AUTH-001 still fires because it only needs LambdaTargets to be non-empty. The impact is graph disconnection, not a missed finding, so low is the right severity.
evidence:
apigateway.py:19 `if not uri or "arn:aws:lambda:" not in uri: return None`; :21-24 slice to '/invocations'. Synthetic run of apigateway._extract_lambda_arn:
  alias    -> arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:<acct>:function:example-fn:prod
  stagevar -> arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:<acct>:function:${stageVariables.fn}
  govcloud -> None ; aws-cn -> None ; http proxy -> None
  dashboard placeholder label for qualified target: 'prod'
  'lambda:'+qualified == 'lambda:'+unqualified FunctionArn ? False
impact: Red and blue teams lose the internet -> API Gateway -> Lambda -> execution-role path whenever integrations target an alias or version, which is common with SAM AutoPublishAlias and stage-variable alias routing. The INVOKES edge ends at a stray node named after the alias. GovCloud and China users get no INVOKES edges at all, but those partitions are unsupported tool-wide anyway.
fix: Parse with a regex such as `arn:(aws[\w-]*):lambda:([^:]+):(\d{12}):function:([^:/]+)(?::([^/]+))?`. Emit the unqualified function ARN as the target and keep the qualifier as an edge attribute (Qualifier). If the name contains '${stageVariables.', resolve it per stage from get_stages()['item'][*]['variables'], or record it as an unresolved target instead of creating a node. Derive the partition from the session (sts.get_caller_identity ARN, or botocore's partition for the region) when building API ARNs at :60 and :94.

title: Avoidable API fan-out: one GetIntegration per REST method (GetResources embed=methods returns it inline) and DescribeTable per DynamoDB table just for the ARN
explanation: apigateway.py:38-48 calls get_integration for every method of every resource. The botocore model shows GetResources accepts embed=['methods'], and Resource.resourceMethods is a map of Method, which includes methodIntegration (uri) and authorizationType. One paginated call (page size up to 500) can therefore replace N GetIntegration calls; this matches documented CLI behaviour and should be confirmed once against a live API. The paginator also runs at the default page size of 25. dynamodb.py:36 calls DescribeTable only to get the TableArn, which is deterministic. Adaptive retries limit the throttling risk, which leaves runtime as the main cost. API Gateway's control-plane quota is about 10 rps per account, so 600 methods take a minute or more per API. If retries are exhausted, apigateway.py:47 `continue` silently drops that Lambda target, which would also suppress APIGW-AUTH-001. The DynamoDB part is minor because DescribeTable quotas are generous.
evidence: apigateway.py:42 `integ = client.get_integration(restApiId=api_id, resourceId=res["id"], httpMethod=method)`. Synthetic API with 200 resources x 3 methods gives calls {'paginate:get_resources': 1, 'get_integration': 600, 'get_authorizers': 1}. botocore apigateway GetResources.embed doc: 'Currently, the request supports only retrieval of the embedded Method resources'. The Method shape includes methodIntegration and authorizationType. dynamodb.py:36 `table_arn = client.describe_table(TableName=name)["Table"].get("TableArn")`.
impact: Large REST APIs make enumeration slow and noisy (many GetIntegration CloudTrail events). Under heavy throttling, Lambda targets can be silently lost.
fix: Use client.get_paginator('get_resources').paginate(restApiId=api_id, embed=['methods'], PaginationConfig={'PageSize': 500}) and read resourceMethods[m].get('methodIntegration', {}).get('uri'). Fall back to get_integration only when methodIntegration is absent. Capture authorizationType at the same time (this enables the P1-060 fix). For DynamoDB, build arn:{partition}:dynamodb:{region}:{account}:table/{name} from a single STS call and drop describe_table, which also removes the DescribeTable-failure drop noted in P1-075.

title: CloudFront collector drops Aliases/CacheBehaviors/OriginGroups/Restrictions/DefaultRootObject, persists origin CustomHeaders secret values, and adds a per-distribution call only to get Logging
explanation: The summary at cloudfront.py:18-33 has no Aliases, CacheBehaviors, OriginGroups, Restrictions, CustomErrorResponses or DefaultRootObject. It stores DistributionConfig.Origins in full, and the Origin shape includes CustomHeaders (HeaderName/HeaderValue). The botocore model shows that DistributionSummary from ListDistributions already contains every collected field except Logging, so the GetDistributionConfig call per distribution (line 17) exists only to fetch Logging. Storing CustomHeaders values conflicts with the tool's own data-minimization stance: k8s.py:143 says 'NAMES + TYPES ONLY - never read values', and the Secrets Manager/SSM collectors do not fetch values. Related observation outside this batch: k8s.py:152 saves every Secret's annotations, and kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration can contain the full Secret data, which contradicts that same comment and is worth a separate issue. Severity stays low. No analyzer reads CloudFront data, so the missing fields only affect manual review and future CloudFront-to-origin or subdomain-takeover analysis.
evidence:
Model: DistributionSummary members include Aliases, Origins, OriginGroups, DefaultCacheBehavior, CacheBehaviors, ViewerCertificate, Restrictions, WebACLId, HttpVersion, IsIPV6Enabled (no Logging, no DefaultRootObject). Origin members include CustomHeaders.
Mock run (scratchpad agents/collectors-core-1/cf_test.py):
  keys: ['ARN','Comment','DefaultCacheBehavior','DomainName','Enabled','HttpVersion','Id','IsIPV6Enabled','Logging','Origins','PriceClass','Status','ViewerCertificate','WebACLId']
  Aliases kept? False | CacheBehaviors kept? False
  CustomHeaders value persisted: True
impact: Custom domains (needed for dangling-CNAME/subdomain-takeover checks and for mapping assets to Route53) and path-routed origins are lost. Origin-verification secrets, which often let an attacker bypass CloudFront/WAF and reach the origin directly, are written in plaintext to report files and zips that operators may share. For the red team that is useful loot. For report handling it is sensitive data the tool's own policy says it avoids.
fix: Build the record from DistributionSummary and add Aliases, CacheBehaviors, OriginGroups, Restrictions and CustomErrorResponses. Call GetDistributionConfig only for Logging and DefaultRootObject, or skip it behind a flag to cut calls. Redact CustomHeaders[].HeaderValue by default (keep HeaderName plus a hash or length) and add an opt-in flag such as --include-secrets. Separately, strip kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration from saved Secret annotations in k8s.py.

title: Inconsistent per-item ClientError handling silently drops resources (SQS, DynamoDB, KMS, ECS, SageMaker; up to 100 CodeBuild projects per failed batch)
explanation: All cited sites are accurate. SNS (sns.py:44-45) and ECR (ecr.py:44-45) keep the resource with Policy=None when the per-item call fails. SQS (sqs.py:39-40), DynamoDB (dynamodb.py:37-38), KMS (kms.py:64-65), ECS (ecs.py:37-38) and SageMaker (sagemaker.py:38-39) `continue` silently and drop the resource. In several cases the identifier is already known without the failing call: the SQS ARN is derivable from the URL, list_keys returns KeyArn, and the DynamoDB ARN is deterministic. CodeBuild drops the whole 100-name batch on a single failure (codebuild.py:38-41). No warning is printed and no marker is written. Denials are realistic: a KMS key policy that does not delegate to IAM denies DescribeKey to the auditor, and hardened SQS policies deny GetQueueAttributes. Drops are silent, but this only affects completeness, so low severity is appropriate.
evidence: Synthetic mocks with per-item AccessDenied: SQS -> resources.json [] ; DynamoDB -> [] ; KMS -> keys.json [] ; CodeBuild with 150 projects where the batch containing one denied project fails -> 50 stored (100 lost). Contrast: sns.py:44-45 and ecr.py:44-45 `except ClientError: pass` keep the item.
impact: Whether a resource appears in the graph depends on which API happened to be denied, with no indication. Locked-down KMS keys and queues (often the interesting ones) vanish, and RDS or EBS encrypted-by edges end at placeholders. CodeBuild PassRole targets can disappear in blocks of 100.
fix: Keep every listed resource. Fill in what is known (SQS ARN from the URL, KeyArn from list_keys, a deterministic DynamoDB ARN, the ECS revision ARN, the SageMaker name) and add 'CollectionError': '<ErrorCode>'. For CodeBuild, on batch failure retry each name individually (or bisect) and record unresolved names. Print a per-module count of partial items.

title: Collectors catch only ClientError: a BotoCoreError (or any other exception) aborts the module and discards everything collected so far
explanation: The mechanism is real. None of the 19 service collectors (lambda_, kms, ecs, cloudformation, glue, codebuild, sagemaker, sns, sqs, ecr, rds, dynamodb, apigateway, cognito, ebs, elb, route53, secretsmanager, ssm) catches BotoCoreError, and nor do iam, s3 or eks. Only vpc, sg and ec2 use safe() (aws_utils.py:19-33). Output is written after the loops, so an exception escaping to run_module (main.py:95-98) leaves no resources.json, and in Cognito the identity-pool failure also skips user pools. Severity is lower than claimed for three reasons. main() sets AWS_RETRY_MODE=adaptive and AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS=10 (main.py:202-203), and adaptive/standard mode retries botocore ConnectionError and HTTPClientError (EndpointConnectionError, ReadTimeoutError, ConnectTimeoutError, ConnectionClosedError) up to 10 times, so transient network blips rarely surface. run_module limits the damage to one module in one region and prints a red '[-] ... module failed' line. Re-running fixes it. Residual triggers are persistent connectivity loss, credential refresh failures (TokenRetrievalError and similar, not retried), ParamValidationError, and plain Python errors.
evidence: cognito.py:54 and :68 `except ClientError as e:`. Synthetic: list_identity_pools paginate raising EndpointConnectionError makes cognito.enumerate raise EndpointConnectionError (a BotoCoreError). resources.json written? False; list_user_pools calls = 0. A failure on the 3rd of 5 pools via run_module prints 'cognito module failed', resources.json written? False. botocore check: EndpointConnectionError, ReadTimeoutError, ConnectTimeoutError and ConnectionClosedError are retryable transient errors; TokenRetrievalError and ParamValidationError are not.
impact: Occasionally a whole service in one region is missing from the report and graph after a persistent network or credential error. The manifest still lists the empty module dir and the parser treats it as 'no resources', so this is easy to miss when reviewing results later.
fix: Define AWS_ERRORS = (ClientError, BotoCoreError) in aws_utils and use it in every collector's except clauses, or route calls through safe(). Make independent sections (Cognito identity vs user pools, API Gateway REST vs HTTP) fully independent. In run_module, on an unexpected exception write a {'Error': ..., 'Partial': true} marker file so the parser and dashboard can show the gap, or have collectors write partial results in a finally block.

title: EBS collector makes one DescribeSnapshotAttribute call per snapshot (and reports Public=false when that call fails)
explanation: The fan-out is real: ebs.py:34-40 issues DescribeSnapshotAttribute for every self-owned snapshot, so 5000 snapshots means 5000 calls. The proposed replacement is incomplete. describe_snapshots(OwnerIds=['self'], RestorableByUserIds=['all']) does return the account's public snapshots in one paginated call (confirmed by the botocore DescribeSnapshots docs: 'all for public snapshots'). It cannot find explicit cross-account shares to unknown account IDs, which the collector also records (SharedAccounts, EBS-XACCT-001), so per-snapshot calls are still needed for that. Adaptive retries with 10 attempts (main.py:202-203) make throttle exhaustion unlikely, so the cost is mostly runtime and CloudTrail volume. The more important adjacent defect: any failure of the attribute call (throttle exhaustion, UnauthorizedOperation, SCP) is swallowed (ebs.py:46-47) and the snapshot is written as Public=false with SharedAccounts=[]. That is a confident negative, not 'unknown'.
evidence: ebs.py:34-40 per-snapshot loop; :46-47 `except ClientError: pass`. Synthetic 5000 snapshots: describe_snapshot_attribute calls: 5000. A snapshot whose attribute call raised RequestLimitExceeded, and one that raised UnauthorizedOperation, were both stored as {'Public': False, 'SharedAccounts': [], ...}.
impact: In accounts with AWS Backup or DLM, enumeration of each region can take many minutes and produces thousands of DescribeSnapshotAttribute events, which is noisy for red-team use. If the attribute call is denied or throttled, public or shared snapshots are silently reported as private, so EBS-PUB-001 and EBS-XACCT-001 are missed.
fix: First run describe_snapshots(OwnerIds=['self'], RestorableByUserIds=['all']) to mark public snapshots cheaply. Keep per-snapshot DescribeSnapshotAttribute only for cross-account detection, optionally behind a flag or cap, and use a thread pool sized to the EC2 rate limit. On a per-snapshot failure record 'PermissionsUnknown': true (or Public: null) instead of false, and have the parser surface the gap. Optionally read GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState once per region for context.

title: EC2, VPC and S3 collectors miss attacker-relevant fields (UserData, KeyName, IPv6/secondary public IPs, EIPs, TGW/VPN, account-level PAB, policy status)
explanation: ec2.py:42-62 keeps a fixed subset of instance fields. KeyName and Ipv6Address are dropped, though DescribeInstances returns them at no extra cost. The ENI mapping (ec2.py:30-40) drops Association.PublicIp and Ipv6Addresses. No call is made for UserData (DescribeInstanceAttribute), describe_addresses, launch templates or SSM DescribeInstanceInformation. vpc.py:13-23 has no Transit Gateway, VPN, Network Firewall or endpoint-service calls. s3.py:58-137 makes 10 per-bucket calls but no s3control account-level PAB, GetBucketPolicyStatus, ownership controls, website or replication. The IPv6 example holds: _check_sg_public_access already treats ::/0 as public (policy_parser.py:1256-1261), but exposure findings require PublicIpAddress, so an instance reachable only over IPv6 is never flagged. Related: S3-PUBLIC-001 (policy_parser.py:997-1025) ignores the bucket-level PAB that is collected and the account-level PAB that is not, so public-bucket findings can be false positives. Severity stays low because these are scope gaps, not defects in existing logic.
evidence:
ec2.py:42-62 instance_data has no KeyName, Ipv6Address or UserData. ec2.py:30-40 ENI dict has no Association or Ipv6Addresses.
grep -rn 'describe_addresses|launch_template|describe_instance_information|transit_gateway|vpn|network_firewall|s3control|policy_status|ownership|bucket_website|replication' app/components (excluding the parser): no collector hits.
policy_parser.py:1460  has_public_ip = bool(inst.get('PublicIpAddress')) gates exposure findings.
impact: IPv6-only and secondary-ENI exposure is invisible (false negatives). Secrets in UserData, a classic red-team find, are never surfaced. Lateral routes over TGW/VPN are missing from the network picture. S3 public findings can be wrong in both directions without account-level PAB and policy status.
fix: Keep KeyName, Ipv6Address, ENI Association.PublicIp and Ipv6Addresses (free). Add describe_addresses, describe_launch_templates plus versions (UserData), optional per-instance DescribeInstanceAttribute userData behind a flag, ssm describe_instance_information, TGW/VPN/Network Firewall describes, s3control get_public_access_block, and get_bucket_policy_status/ownership_controls. Make exposure logic consider IPv6 and ENI public IPs, and make S3-PUBLIC-001 honor PAB.

title: IMDS false positive: HttpEndpoint is not captured, so instances with IMDS disabled are still flagged IMDSv1/SSRF and given an SSRF_TO_IMDS edge
explanation: ec2.py:56-59 keeps only HttpTokens and HttpPutResponseHopLimit from MetadataOptions and drops HttpEndpoint. policy_parser.py:1520-1521 raises EC2-IMDS-001 whenever HttpTokens == 'optional'. The dashboard also marks the node vulnerable (index.html:1133), adds an SSRF_TO_IMDS edge (index.html:1246-1247), and shows 'NOT ENFORCED' (index.html:2450). An end-to-end synthetic run reproduced it: an instance with HttpEndpoint=disabled and HttpTokens=optional is saved without HttpEndpoint and gets EC2-IMDS-001. The reviewer understated the scope slightly, since the graph also gets a false edge, not only a finding. Severity stays low because this configuration is uncommon.
impact: Instances with IMDS turned off appear as SSRF-to-credential paths in both findings and the attack graph, which wastes red-team effort and adds remediation noise for blue teams.
fix: In ec2.py, store the full MetadataOptions (HttpEndpoint, HttpTokens, HttpPutResponseHopLimit, HttpProtocolIpv6, InstanceMetadataTags, State). In policy_parser.py:1521 and index.html:1133/1246/2450, require HttpEndpoint != 'disabled' (treat a missing value as enabled for older reports). Optionally raise severity when HopLimit > 1, since containers can then reach IMDS.

title: Unpaginated list calls (EKS nodegroups/fargate/addons, WAF rule groups/IP sets/logging configs, IAM list_*_policies, S3 ListBuckets)
explanation: The cited calls do ignore pagination: eks.py:64,81,98, waf.py:92,115,137, iam.py:324,347,370 and s3.py:33. WAF web ACLs are paginated correctly (waf.py:40-82). Practical impact is much smaller than the report suggests, because service quotas keep counts under one page. EKS defaults to 30 managed node groups and 10 Fargate profiles per cluster, and the add-on catalog is far below 100. WAFv2 defaults to 100 rule groups and 100 IP sets per Region. IAM inline-policy aggregate size limits (2,048 characters for users, 5,120 for groups, 10,240 for roles) make more than 100 inline policies per entity practically impossible. The S3 claim is accurate but narrow: botocore 1.37.34 docs say unpaginated ListBuckets is rejected only for accounts with an approved general-purpose bucket quota above 10,000. In that case s3.py:35-38 catches the ClientError and writes {'Error'}, so the whole S3 module, including S3 attack edges, is lost loudly rather than silently. EKS paginators exist for all three ops; wafv2 has no botocore paginators, so NextMarker must be looped manually.
evidence:
eks.py:64  ng_resp = eks_client.list_nodegroups(clusterName=name)   (no nextToken loop; model: maxResults 1-100)
waf.py:92  response = client.list_rule_groups(Scope=scope)   (NextMarker ignored)
s3.py:33  buckets_response = s3_client.list_buckets()   (botocore ListBuckets paginator exists: ContinuationToken/MaxBuckets)
S3 model doc: 'All unpaginated ListBuckets requests will be rejected for Amazon Web Services accounts with a general purpose bucket quota greater than 10,000.'
impact: Very large S3 estates lose all S3 data and S3 attack edges, with an Error recorded. Elsewhere, truncation only occurs when quotas have been raised. WAF data is not analyzed anyway, and the IAM part is effectively unreachable.
fix: Use session paginators: s3 get_paginator('list_buckets'), eks get_paginator('list_nodegroups'/'list_fargate_profiles'/'list_addons'), iam get_paginator('list_user_policies'/'list_role_policies'/'list_group_policies'). Add a NextMarker loop for wafv2 list_rule_groups, list_ip_sets and list_logging_configurations, reusing the web ACL loop pattern.

title: Documentation drift: IAM/S3 docstrings and README report tree are out of date, and README 'Run directly' installs only boto3 (kubernetes missing, so K8s collection fails)
explanation: The iam.py:13-29 docstring tree has no instance_profiles.json, which iam.py:429 writes and policy_parser.py:1297-1302 depends on. The s3.py:8-17 docstring has no notifications/, which s3.py:43 and :131-135 create. readme.md:94 ('Run directly') runs only 'pip install boto3', while pyproject.toml and requirements.txt both declare kubernetes. Without it, app/utils/eks_auth.py:64 (the reviewer's cited path app/components/eks_auth.py does not exist) raises ModuleNotFoundError, k8s.py:61-68 records auth_status 'failed' for every cluster, and the whole K8s/IRSA analysis is empty. The README tree point is weaker than stated because readme.md:143 describes iam/ in prose, not as a file list. The README drift is actually broader: the report tree (readme.md:141-158) leaves out 19 modules (secretsmanager, ssm, lambda, kms, ecs, cloudformation, glue, codebuild, sagemaker, sns, sqs, ecr, rds, dynamodb, apigateway, cognito, ebs, elb, route53) and several analysis/*_relationships.json files, and it says global/ holds 'IAM, S3, CloudFront' when route53 and waf_cloudfront also go there. The repo .venv lacking kubernetes is local, gitignored environment state and does not affect users.
evidence:
iam.py:13-29 tree lists no instance_profiles.json; iam.py:429 writes it.
readme.md:92-96: git clone ...; cd aws-enumerator; pip install boto3; python app/main.py --region eu-west-2
pyproject.toml dependencies = ["boto3", "kubernetes"]; requirements.txt has boto3 and kubernetes; Dockerfile:7 installs -r requirements.txt.
.venv/bin/python -c 'import kubernetes' -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'kubernetes'
impact: Users who follow the 'Run directly' instructions silently get no Kubernetes or IRSA data, and the only sign is auth_status 'failed' in cluster_info.json. Out-of-date report-structure docs mislead people writing integrations or reviewing reports.
fix: Change readme.md:94 to 'pip install -r requirements.txt'. Have k8s.py print a clear warning, or skip with auth_status 'skipped: kubernetes package not installed', when the import fails. Update the iam.py/s3.py docstrings and regenerate the README report tree from the actual module list (including the global/ contents and analysis files).
also_reported_as: README, module docstrings and attack_paths.md lag the 16 collectors and 6 analysers added on this branch

title: High-volume N+1 collection (IAM per-entity instead of GAAD, 10 S3 calls per bucket, 1 ENI call per SG) with error bursts and no request budget or resume
explanation: These are merged because both describe the per-entity IAM call pattern instead of one GetAccountAuthorizationDetails, with the same fix. Call counts are mostly right. Each user gets 6 calls, not about 7: list_access_keys :100, list_mfa_devices :114, get_login_profile :127, list_groups_for_user :144, list_attached_user_policies :151 and list_user_policies :324, plus get_user_policy per inline policy. Roles and groups get 2 each. Each local policy gets 1 call (:246) and each AWS-managed attached policy gets 2 (:296-297). S3 makes exactly 10 calls per bucket (s3.py:59-131), several of which return NoSuch* errors. sg.py:29-35 makes one DescribeNetworkInterfaces per SG. get_login_profile returns NoSuchEntity for every non-console user. No budget, rate-limit, resume or offline-GAAD option exists; main.py:202-203 only sets AWS_RETRY_MODE and AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS. The user-agent claim is overstated: botocore always sends cfg/retry-mode#<mode>, and the tool changes it from the default 'legacy' to 'adaptive' rather than adding a token. That makes it a weak fingerprint next to the Boto3 UA itself, and os.environ.setdefault lets operators override it. GAAD is also not a pure opsec win, because it is a single well-known high-signal API. Severity drops to low: noise is inherent to an enumerator, the docs make no stealth claim, and the main concrete gain from GAAD is correctness (P1-033/P1-092/P1-048) and speed.
evidence:
iam.py per-user calls at :100,:114,:127,:144,:151 (+:324 in _enumerate_inline_policies). s3.py per-bucket: get_bucket_location, policy, acl, public_access_block, versioning, encryption, tagging, logging, cors, notification_configuration = 10.
UA check (OS/lang redacted): default -> cfg/retry-mode#legacy; with AWS_RETRY_MODE=adaptive -> 'Boto3/1.37.34 md/Botocore#1.37.34 ua/2.1 ... cfg/retry-mode#adaptive Botocore/1.37.34'. botocore/useragent.py:541-542 always emits cfg retry-mode.
main.py:202-203 setdefault AWS_RETRY_MODE/AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS only.
impact: On large accounts, runs are slow and draw throttling. CloudTrail fills with bursts of IAM/S3 read and NoSuch* error events that anomalous-discovery detections can flag. Without resume, a run interrupted by credential expiry or throttling must start over.
fix: Replace per-entity IAM calls with the get_account_authorization_details paginator, which also fixes P1-033/P1-092/P1-048. Keep the per-user credential calls (access keys, MFA, login profile) optional, or use GenerateCredentialReport/GetCredentialReport, which is one call. Replace per-SG ENI lookups with one paginated describe_network_interfaces grouped by Groups[].GroupId. Make S3 sub-calls selectable. Add --max-requests-per-minute (botocore Config max_pool / token bucket), --resume (skip modules whose output exists) and --gaad-file for offline import. Document the AWS_RETRY_MODE override.

title: IAM collects only default policy versions and skips alternate credentials, last-used data, federation providers and SCPs
explanation: _enumerate_policies (iam.py:243-249) and _enumerate_attached_policy_documents (iam.py:296-297) fetch only DefaultVersionId. app/ has no list_policy_versions, get_access_key_last_used, list_ssh_public_keys, list_service_specific_credentials, list_signing_certificates, list_saml_providers, list_open_id_connect_providers or organizations calls. RoleLastUsed is also missing because ListRoles does not return it (same root cause as P1-033). PRIVESC-002 SetDefaultPolicyVersion (policy_parser.py:35-38) is matched on the action alone. Without the version inventory it fires even when no more-permissive non-default version exists, which can be a false positive, and it cannot point to the dormant version an attacker would activate. Missing OIDC/SAML providers also means federated trust cannot be resolved (see the IRSA issue). SCPs are only readable from the management or delegated-admin account, so that part is a reasonable but limited ask.
evidence:
iam.py:243  version_id = policy.get('DefaultVersionId', 'v1'); :246 get_policy_version(PolicyArn, VersionId=version_id)
iam.py:296-297  get_policy(...)['Policy']['DefaultVersionId'] -> get_policy_version(default)
grep for the APIs listed above across app/: no hits.
policy_parser.py:35  {"id": "PRIVESC-002", "name": "SetDefaultPolicyVersion", "actions": ["iam:SetDefaultPolicyVersion"], ...}
impact: SetDefaultPolicyVersion paths cannot be validated, either as false positives or as hidden admin versions. Stale or unused credentials, SSH/CodeCommit or service-specific credentials, and federation entry points (SAML/OIDC) are missing from the graph. Effective permissions ignore SCP guardrails.
fix: Use GetAccountAuthorizationDetails, which returns PolicyVersionList with every version for local managed policies plus RoleLastUsed, or call list_policy_versions and get_policy_version for each local policy. Make PRIVESC-002 report the non-default versions and escalate only if one grants more than the default. Add get_access_key_last_used, list_ssh_public_keys, list_service_specific_credentials, list_signing_certificates, list_saml_providers and list_open_id_connect_providers. Collect SCPs when organizations:ListPolicies is permitted and model them as a cap.

title: IAM inline-policy List failures are swallowed with no marker (except ClientError: pass)
explanation: For users, roles and groups, a ClientError from list_user_policies, list_role_policies or list_group_policies hits `except ClientError: pass` (iam.py:340-341, 363-364, 386-387). No file is written and nothing is printed, so _load_inline_policies (policy_parser.py:278-295) sees the same thing as 'no inline policies'. Failures of get_*_policy, by contrast, are recorded as {"Error"} entries. I rated it low rather than medium because the trigger is narrow: the principal must be allowed ListRoles/ListAttachedRolePolicies but denied ListRolePolicies, through resource-scoped grants, boundaries or SCPs. Throttling is largely absorbed by AWS_RETRY_MODE=adaptive with AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS=10 (main.py:202-203), and a NoSuchEntity race on a deleted role is benign. It is related to P1-036 (same swallow-without-marker pattern) but in a different module.
evidence: iam.py:340-341 `except ClientError:\n    pass` (likewise 363-364 and 386-387). Repro with list_role_policies raising AccessDenied: 'inline files: NONE (no marker)', and no console output. When allowed: ['inline_policies/roles/roleA.json','inline_policies/roles/roleB.json'].
impact: Inline-granted privesc conditions (e.g. iam:PassRole or iam:* in a role inline policy) are silently missed under certain partial permissions, and the operator gets no hint that coverage is incomplete.
fix: On ClientError, write inline_policies/<type>/<name>.json as {"Error": str(e)}, or add the entity to an errors file, and print a warning. Have the parser flag such entities as 'inline policies unknown'. Also record get_*_policy errors in coverage output instead of dropping them silently at policy_parser.py:400/446/482.

title: Collectors persist sensitive metadata no analyzer uses (all DNS record values, SSM LastModifiedUser, secret descriptions/tags)
explanation: route53.py:55-59 stores every record's values, including TXT and internal A values, in resources.json (:66-74). The only consumer is policy_parser.py:3175-3184, which reads TakeoverCandidates only, and the dashboard never reads route53/resources.json (it loads only analysis/*.json, IAM files, s3/buckets.json and ec2/instances.json; index.html:994-1040). ssm.py:32-33 dumps the raw ParameterMetadata, which includes LastModifiedUser (with SSO, the session name is often an email), Description and Policies. The parser uses only Name, ARN, Type and KeyId. secretsmanager.py:47-48 dumps the raw SecretListEntry, including Description and Tags, while the parser uses ARN, Name and KmsKeyId. The claim is wrong in one detail: SecretListEntry has no LastModifiedUser field (botocore model), so that PII exists only in SSM output. The incremental sensitivity is also modest. Public-zone TXT values (SPF, DKIM, verification tokens) are publicly resolvable already, and the report already contains IAM, VPC and IP topology by design. The real additions are private-zone hostnames and IPs, principal identities (emails) and free-text descriptions. lambda_.py:5-6 states the aim that the report 'stays safe to share', so data minimisation fits the tool's own intent.
evidence: A synthetic private-zone run persisted Records such as ('TXT', ['"verification-token=PLACEHOLDER"']) and ('A', ['10.0.0.5']), and parser findings used only TakeoverCandidates. botocore ParameterMetadata members include 'LastModifiedUser', 'Description' and 'Policies'. SecretListEntry members include 'Description' and 'Tags' and have no LastModifiedUser. Parser field use: secret.get('ARN'|'KmsKeyId'), param.get('Name'|'ARN'|'Type'|'KeyId') (policy_parser.py ~1766-1845).
impact: Shared reports leak internal DNS topology, operator identities and free-text secret descriptions or tags, which sometimes hold hints, at no analytic benefit. The risk to operators and their clients is small but avoidable.
fix:
Project to analysed fields only.
- Route53: store only Name, Type and the alias or CNAME target, and omit values for TXT, MX and SRV records and for A records in private zones, unless a `--full-dns` flag is set.
- SSM: keep Name, ARN, Type, KeyId, Tier, DataType and Version.
- Secrets Manager: keep ARN, Name, KmsKeyId, RotationEnabled, LastRotatedDate, LastAccessedDate, OwningService and PrimaryRegion.
Put Description, Tags and LastModifiedUser behind an opt-in flag.

title: Compute collectors cover only 5 PassRole targets; existing-role hijack surfaces (SageMaker Studio, ECS Exec, CodeBuild webhooks, StackSets) not collected
explanation: The facts are accurate. sagemaker.py:24-26 lists only notebook instances. glue.py covers jobs and dev endpoints only. ecs.py:24 covers task definitions only. cloudformation.py:25 calls describe_stacks only. codebuild.py:42-49 keeps only arn, name and serviceRole, and discards the `webhook` and `source` fields that batch_get_projects already returns. COMPUTE_ACTIONS (policy_parser.py:2567-2573) and PRIVESC-016..020 (:111-138) match this scope. The framing conflates two different gaps, though. For classic PassRole escalation (create a new training or processing job, a Glue session, or a stack set with a passed role), enumerating existing resources adds little: the missing piece is IAM rules such as iam:PassRole + sagemaker:CreateTrainingJob/CreateProcessingJob/CreateModel or glue:CreateSession, not collectors. Transform jobs take no RoleArn; they use the model's role. The collector gap that matters for the graph is resources whose existing role can be taken over without PassRole. SageMaker Studio user profiles and domains can be entered via CreatePresignedDomainUrl. ECS services or tasks with enableExecuteCommand can be entered via ecs:ExecuteCommand. CodeBuild webhooks and source credentials enable poisoned-pipeline attacks. Self-managed StackSets have Administration and Execution roles. The README advertises exactly the 20 rules it implements, so this is a scope gap rather than a defect.
evidence: sagemaker.py:24 `client.get_paginator("list_notebook_instances")`; codebuild.py:43-49 keeps only `p.get("serviceRole")`, `arn` and `name`; ecs.py:24 `list_task_definitions`; cloudformation.py:25 `describe_stacks`. A grep of app/, docs/ and README for CreateTrainingJob|CreatePresignedDomainUrl|CreateSession|StackSet|ExecuteCommand|webhook found no matches.
impact: The attack graph has no edges for several well-known role takeover paths, such as Studio presigned URLs, ECS Exec and CodeBuild pipeline poisoning. Red and blue teams therefore under-count principals that can reach privileged roles.
fix:
Prioritise surfaces that let an existing role be taken over:
- SageMaker: list_domains, list_user_profiles and describe_user_profile/describe_domain (ExecutionRole, including DefaultUserSettings). Add USES_ROLE edges, plus CAN_MODIFY for sagemaker:CreatePresignedDomainUrl.
- ECS: list_clusters, list_services and describe_services (enableExecuteCommand, taskDefinition). Add an ecs:ExecuteCommand edge to the task role.
- CodeBuild: keep `webhook`, `source.type`, `source.location` and `source.auth.type`, and call list_source_credentials (metadata only).
- CloudFormation: list_stack_sets and describe_stack_set (AdministrationRoleARN, ExecutionRoleName).
For ephemeral jobs, add PRIVESC rules instead of collectors: PassRole with sagemaker:CreateTrainingJob, CreateProcessingJob or CreateModel, and PassRole with glue:CreateSession.

title: Secret resource-policy filenames come from secret names: '/'/'_' collisions overwrite policies and >~250-char names abort the loop
explanation: Both issues come from the same line, the per-secret file path `f"{policies_dir}/{_safe_filename(secret_name)}.json"` (secretsmanager.py:70, helper at :17-19). (a) Collision: Secrets Manager names allow '/' and '_' (botocore model: ASCII letters, digits and /_+=.@-). ':' and space are not legal, so the only real collapse is '/' to '_'. 'prod/db' and 'prod_db' therefore map to one file and the last write wins. The loader keys by SecretArn (policy_parser.py:1694-1700), so the overwritten secret's policy disappears and SECRET-PUB-001 or SECRET-XAUTH-001 can be lost. Which secret survives depends on listing order. (b) Long names: names can be up to 512 characters, and since '/' is flattened the whole name becomes one path component. Above about 250 characters open() raises OSError ENAMETOOLONG, which `except ClientError` (:76) does not catch. The crash needs the long-named secret to actually have a resource policy, because no file is written otherwise. When it fires, enumerate() aborts: secrets.json is already written (:47-48), but the policies of every later secret are lost. main.run_module (main.py:89-98) catches the exception and prints '[-] secretsmanager module failed', so the failure is visible to the operator, not silent, and the rest of the run continues. Both triggers are uncommon in practice, so overall severity is low even though the consequence is a missed HIGH finding.
evidence:
Mock collision test:
- Secrets 'prod/db' (Principal '*') and 'prod_db' (same-account root) produced files ['prod_db.json'], which contains only prod_db, and parser findings were [].
- Reversing the listing order gives ['SECRET-PUB-001'], so the outcome depends on order.
Long-name test (300-char name with a cross-account policy, then 'normal' with a public policy), run through main.run_module:
- Output was '[-] secretsmanager module failed: [Errno 63] File name too long', secrets.json was written, and resource_policies/ was [], so the public 'normal' policy was lost.
- With the same long name but no policy there is no crash, and the 'normal.json' file was written.
impact: There are rare false negatives on secret public or cross-account exposure. The collision could also be used deliberately: someone able to create a colliding secret name could hide a public policy from the tool. The long-name case loses all remaining secret policies for that region but announces the failure.
fix: Stop deriving filenames from names. Write `resource_policies/<sha256(SecretArn)[:16]>.json`, since the file already carries SecretArn and SecretName and the loader keys by SecretArn, so no parser change is needed. Alternatively, store all policies in a single resource_policies.json keyed by ARN. Also wrap the per-secret write in `except (ClientError, OSError)` so that one bad item cannot abort the loop. Apply the same hashing to lambda_.py:19-21/104 for consistency, since case-insensitive filesystems such as macOS can collide names that differ only in case.

title: SQS ListQueues paginator never sends MaxResults, silently truncating at 1,000 queues per region
explanation: sqs.py:24-25 calls `client.get_paginator("list_queues").paginate()` with no PaginationConfig. The botocore paginator for ListQueues uses limit_key MaxResults, which is sent only when PageSize is set. The ListQueues and MaxResults documentation in botocore 1.37.34 says that without MaxResults the response holds at most 1,000 results and no NextToken ('You must set MaxResults to receive a value for NextToken'). Pagination therefore stops after the first page, no warning is printed, and the collector reports success. Severity is lowered to low because only regions with more than 1,000 queues in a single account are affected. For those accounts the loss is silent and deterministic, and the fix is one line.
evidence:
botocore model: paginator OrderedDict(input_token='NextToken', limit_key='MaxResults', output_token='NextToken', result_key='QueueUrls'). The MaxResults doc reads 'You must set MaxResults to receive a value for NextToken in the response.'
Stubber with list_queues expected_params={} returning 1,000 URLs and no NextToken: sqs.enumerate wrote 1,000 queues and the stub assertion passed, which proves MaxResults is not sent.
With PaginationConfig={'PageSize':1000}, MaxResults=1000 is sent and NextToken is followed: 1,001 URLs across 2 pages.
impact: In large accounts, queues beyond the first 1,000 have no policy analysis. Public or cross-account SQS grants and their graph edges are missed, and the run gives no indication of it.
fix: `for page in paginator.paginate(PaginationConfig={"PageSize": 1000}):` in sqs.py:25. Optionally log when a page returns exactly 1,000 URLs without a NextToken.

title: Uncollected exposure surfaces: public SSM documents, SNS subscriptions/SSE, SQS SSE, ECR registry policy, Lambda layer policies/ESMs, AMI launch permissions
explanation:
Most items are accurate:
- No module calls list_documents or describe_document_permission, so public SSM documents (a real secret-leak vector) are not detected.
- sns.py:37-38 reads only attrs['Policy'], although GetTopicAttributes also returns KmsMasterKeyId. There is no list_subscriptions_by_topic call, so external or cross-account subscription endpoints are not collected.
- sqs.py:37 requests only ["QueueArn","Policy"], so KmsMasterKeyId and SqsManagedSseEnabled are not collected.
- ecr.py has no get_registry_policy or describe_registry call.
- lambda_.py has no layer-policy or event-source-mapping calls; it stores layer ARNs only (:37).
- ec2.py has no describe_images or describe_image_attribute call, so public or shared AMIs are not detected.
- secretsmanager.py:32 paginates list_secrets without IncludePlannedDeletion, which defaults to excluding secrets scheduled for deletion.
One item is mis-framed. DescribeParameters `Shared=True` lists parameters shared WITH the account (inbound, a lateral-movement signal), not the account's parameters shared out. Outbound exposure needs ssm:GetResourcePolicies on advanced-tier parameters. The value of secrets pending deletion is also low, because they cannot be read until restored.
evidence: botocore DescribeParameters `Shared` doc: 'Lists parameters that are shared with you.' ListSecrets `IncludePlannedDeletion` doc: 'By default, secrets scheduled for deletion aren't included.' A grep for describe_images|image_attribute|registry|list_documents|document_permission|subscriptions|event_source in app/components found no collector calls. sqs.py:37 `AttributeNames=["QueueArn", "Policy"]`; sns.py:38 `policy_str = attrs.get("Policy")`.
impact: Public AMIs and SSM documents (data-leak vectors), SNS subscription endpoints (exfiltration paths) and event-source-mapping data flows are invisible in the graph. Missing SSE key links make KMS blast-radius edges incomplete for SNS and SQS.
fix:
Add each surface as an independent block that tolerates errors:
- SSM: list_documents(Filters=[{Key:'Owner',Values:['Self']}]) + describe_document_permission(PermissionType='Share'), where 'all' means public; get_resource_policies for advanced parameters; optionally describe_parameters(Shared=True) as a separate inbound list.
- SNS: keep KmsMasterKeyId and call list_subscriptions_by_topic (Protocol, Endpoint, Owner).
- SQS: add 'KmsMasterKeyId' and 'SqsManagedSseEnabled' to AttributeNames.
- ECR: get_registry_policy and describe_registry.
- Lambda: list_layers, list_layer_versions and get_layer_version_policy, plus list_event_source_mappings.
- EC2: describe_images(Owners=['self']) + describe_image_attribute(Attribute='launchPermission').
- Secrets Manager: list_secrets(IncludePlannedDeletion=True), recording DeletedDate.
Add matching parser findings and edges (for example AMI-PUB-001, SSMDOC-PUB-001 and SNS/SQS ENCRYPTED_BY edges).

title: EC2/VPC/SG Describe calls never follow NextToken
explanation: Code fact: describe_instances (ec2.py:14), the nine VPC describes (vpc.py:13-26) and describe_security_groups/describe_network_interfaces (sg.py:13, 31) are each called once with no MaxResults, and NextToken is ignored, although client.can_paginate() is True for all 12 operations (the claim says 13). If a NextToken came back, later pages would be dropped silently (stub confirms). However, AWS documentation for these legacy EC2 APIs says unpaginated requests return everything. DescribeSecurityGroups: 'If this parameter is not specified, then all items are returned'. DescribeInstances: 'If you do not specify instance IDs or filters, the output includes information for all instances'. DescribeNetworkInterfaces is called with a group-id filter, which the docs list as an allowed alternative to pagination. So silent truncation is unlikely in practice. The '1,000-item cap' for DescribeVpcEndpoints applies to an explicit MaxResults value, and whether unpaginated responses for the newer APIs (VPC endpoints, NAT gateways) ever carry NextToken cannot be settled statically. That would need a live account with more than 1,000 such resources in one region. The more realistic failure on very large accounts is a timeout or throttle on the unpaginated call, which safe() turns into a silent [] (see P1-036).
evidence: vpc.py:26 `data = safe(f"VPC {key}", lambda c=call, k=key: c()[k], default=[])`. Stub returning {'Vpcs':[vpc-00000001],'NextToken':'page2'}: vpcs.json = [{"VpcId":"vpc-00000001"}], describe_vpcs calls: 1. botocore model docs quoted above, from the installed botocore 1.37.34.
impact: Low likelihood of missing resources. The main real risk is large-account timeouts producing empty files, which feeds the denied-equals-empty problem.
fix: Use paginators everywhere, e.g. `[x for p in ec2.get_paginator('describe_vpcs').paginate() for x in p['Vpcs']]` and likewise for instances (flatten Reservations), security groups and the network interfaces lookup. That also bounds per-request size and avoids timeouts.

title: WAF ListResourcesForWebACL uses invalid ResourceType 'CLOUDFRONT' and checks only ALB for REGIONAL
explanation: waf.py:69-72 passes ResourceType='CLOUDFRONT' for the CloudFront scope. That value is not in the botocore enum (APPLICATION_LOAD_BALANCER, API_GATEWAY, APPSYNC, COGNITO_USER_POOL, APP_RUNNER_SERVICE, VERIFIED_ACCESS_INSTANCE, AMPLIFY), and the API docs say not to use this call for CloudFront. botocore does not validate enums client-side, so the request goes out and fails server-side. The exception is caught at waf.py:75, which sets acl_detail['Error'] and leaves no AssociatedResources. Rules and DefaultAction survive, because update() runs before the association call. For REGIONAL only ALB is queried, so associations with API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito and the other types are missing. Impact is lower than claimed: nothing in policy_parser.py or the dashboard reads WAF output (grep finds no consumer), so no finding or graph edge can say a resource is 'unprotected'. CloudFront association is also captured independently via WebACLId in cloudfront.py:29.
evidence: waf.py:69-72 `assoc = client.list_resources_for_web_acl(WebACLArn=acl["ARN"], ResourceType="CLOUDFRONT" if scope == "CLOUDFRONT" else "APPLICATION_LOAD_BALANCER")`. botocore model enum printed locally; ParamValidator on ResourceType='CLOUDFRONT' gives has_errors() False. Doc: 'For Amazon CloudFront, don't use this call. Instead, use ... ListDistributionsByWebACLId.'
impact: Raw web_acls.json is misleading for human readers: CloudFront ACLs show an Error and non-ALB associations are missing. The attack graph and findings are unaffected today.
fix: For CLOUDFRONT, skip the call and derive associations from cloudfront distributions' WebACLId, or call cloudfront.list_distributions_by_web_acl_id. For REGIONAL, loop over every enum ResourceType with per-type try/except (each needs service-specific permissions) and merge the results. Move the association call into its own try so its failure does not mark the whole ACL as errored.

title: Partition hard-coding: commercial STS host in EKS token, us-east-1 global session, aws-only region regex and ARNs
explanation: Confirmed parts: (1) eks_auth.py:34 hard-codes https://sts.{region}.amazonaws.com/. That is correct for aws-us-gov (botocore resolves sts.us-gov-west-1.amazonaws.com) but wrong for aws-cn (sts.cn-north-1.amazonaws.com.cn), so EKS auth fails in China. (2) main.py:221 uses get_boto3_session('us-east-1') for the --all global phase. With GovCloud or China credentials, the global IAM/S3/CloudFront/WAF/Route53 modules fail, and get_enabled_regions (main.py:227, not wrapped in run_module) raises, aborting the whole --all run. waf.py:32 also forces us-east-1. (3) The dashboard regex at index.html:1031 does not match us-gov-* (or us-iso-*) folder names. It does match cn-*. It is used only to gather EC2 instances in --all mode. The parser also builds 11 'arn:aws:' ARNs (e.g. policy_parser.py:1018, 1636, 2318, 3132). Overstated parts: single-region GovCloud (--region us-gov-west-1) mostly works, EKS token included, so 'effectively unsupported' is too strong for GovCloud. P1-054's second claim, that one token per cluster might expire partway through, is speculative. The token behaves like `aws eks get-token`, valid for about 15 minutes, and each cluster gets only 11 single list calls, so exceeding that is very unlikely.
evidence: eks_auth.py:34 `'url': f'https://sts.{region}.amazonaws.com/'`. Decoded token for cn-north-1: host https://sts.cn-north-1.amazonaws.com/, whereas boto3 sts endpoint_url is https://sts.cn-north-1.amazonaws.com.cn. For us-gov-west-1 the host matches the boto3 endpoint. main.py:221 `global_session = get_boto3_session("us-east-1")`. node regex test: us-gov-west-1 false, cn-north-1 true, eu-west-2 true.
impact: China partition: EKS/K8s enumeration fails and --all crashes. GovCloud: --all crashes and some dashboard data is lost. Commercial partition users are unaffected.
fix: Derive the partition with session.get_partition_for_region(region). Take the STS URL from session.client('sts', region_name=region).meta.endpoint_url. Pick the global-phase region per partition (us-east-1, us-gov-west-1 or cn-north-1). Wrap get_enabled_regions in error handling. Build ARNs with the detected partition. Change the dashboard regex to /^([a-z]{2}(?:-[a-z]+)+-\d+)\//.

title: Kubernetes API client has no connect/read timeout; an unreachable (private or CIDR-restricted) endpoint stalls the run
explanation: build_k8s_client (eks_auth.py:69-73) sets only host, verify_ssl, ssl_ca_cert and api_key. No call in k8s.py passes _request_timeout (grep for timeout/retries in k8s.py and eks_auth.py finds nothing). In the kubernetes Python client, a missing _request_timeout means urllib3 runs with timeout=None, so connect waits for the OS TCP timeout and reads have no bound. Configuration.retries=None leaves urllib3's default Retry(3), so up to 4 connect attempts per cluster. The stall hits only the /version probe (k8s.py:80), because a failure there returns early (k8s.py:88-93), so it costs one stall per unreachable cluster, not 11. That stall can still be several minutes. The field note that Run A failed with MaxRetryError fits this path. The 776 s duration is not attributable without per-module timing. The 'private-endpoint pre-check' idea in P1-045 is optional and should not be a hard skip, because an operator running inside the VPC can reach private endpoints. The kubernetes package is not installed in the venv, so the client defaults come from knowledge of the library source and were not executed.
evidence: eks_auth.py:69-73 Configuration() with host/verify_ssl/ssl_ca_cert/api_key only; k8s.py:80 `version = version_api.get_code()` with no _request_timeout; k8s.py:213-214 skips only clusters missing name, endpoint or CA. clusters.json holds the full describe_cluster output (eks.py:55-56), so resourcesVpcConfig.endpointPublicAccess/publicAccessCidrs is available for a warning.
impact: Runs against accounts with private-only EKS clusters can take minutes longer per cluster and look hung. It is a reliability and usability problem; data is not lost.
fix: Pass `_request_timeout=(5, 60)` (connect, read) on the version probe and every list call, or set `config.retries = 1`. If resourcesVpcConfig.endpointPublicAccess is false, or publicAccessCidrs excludes 0.0.0.0/0, print a hint and use an even shorter connect timeout, but still try.

title: Broad try/except ImportError dual-import fallback makes the final error line misleading on a real import failure
explanation: main.py:10-25 wraps `from app.components import (...)` in `except ImportError:` and retries `from components import (...)`. The same pattern appears in ec2.py:1-4, sg.py:1-4, vpc.py:1-4 and k8s.py:26-29. In package mode (pipx console script), any real ImportError inside a component falls through to the fallback, whose final line is `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'components'`. The reviewers overstate it as 'masks/hides': Python prints the chained traceback ('During handling of the above exception...'), and the real cause appears first. The fallback is load-bearing, because the Docker ENTRYPOINT `python app/main.py` (Dockerfile:18) and the README's 'python app/main.py' rely on it. No component currently imports an optional third-party module at top level (kubernetes is imported lazily in k8s.py), so a realistic trigger today is rare.
evidence: `python -c "import sys; sys.modules['app.components.route53']=None; import app.main"` -> first traceback: `ModuleNotFoundError: import of app.components.route53 halted; None in sys.modules` at main.py:11; then 'During handling...'; final: main.py:19 `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'components'`.
impact: Contributors and users debugging a broken install see a misleading last line. Operational impact is minimal.
fix: Standardise on package execution: in the Dockerfile `pip install .` and use `ENTRYPOINT ["aws-enumerator"]` (or `python -m app.main`), and update the README. Then delete all fallbacks. If script mode must stay, narrow the handler to `except ModuleNotFoundError as e: if e.name not in ('app', 'app.components', 'app.utils'): raise`.

title: Version hard-coded at 0.2.0 in main.py, pyproject and dashboard while CI publishes v0.2.N; report provenance lost
explanation: VERSION = "0.2.0" (main.py:27) has stayed unchanged since d55d935 and is written into manifest.json (main.py:69) and the banner (:34). pyproject.toml:7 also says 0.2.0, and the dashboard hard-codes `v0.2.0` (index.html:586), a fourth source. CI computes MAJOR=0/MINOR=2 (docker-publish.yml:8-9) plus a tag count (:30-31). `git ls-remote --tags origin` lists v0.2.0 through v0.2.6 plus a non-v-prefixed 0.1.0, and the only local tag is `0.1.0`. All 20 local manifests that carry a version report 0.2.0, even though the code generations produce different analysis file sets. A manifest therefore cannot identify the build or commit that produced a report. The two reports describe the same root cause, so they are merged. The severity is low (provenance and debugging), not medium.
evidence: main.py:27 `VERSION = "0.2.0"`; pyproject.toml:7 `version = "0.2.0"`; index.html:586 `v0.2.0`; docker-publish.yml:8-9, :30-31; remote tags v0.2.0..v0.2.6 and 0.1.0; local `git tag -l` -> 0.1.0 only.
impact: Blue and red teams comparing reports cannot tell which analysis semantics produced a finding set, for example before and after the noise fix, or with or without the --all ordering bug. Bug reports cannot be tied to a build.
fix: Use a single source of truth: derive the version from git tags (setuptools-scm) or from importlib.metadata.version('aws-enumerator'). Have CI pass `--build-arg VERSION`/`GIT_SHA` and write `version` and `git_sha` into manifest.json. Have the dashboard read the version from the manifest. Retag 0.1.0 as v0.1.0 for consistency.

title: Reports embed operator identity and are written with default umask (world-readable) and unencrypted zips
explanation: generate_manifest writes caller_arn and caller_user_id (main.py:76-77). For SSO or assumed-role sessions these usually contain the session name, often an email. Folders are created with os.makedirs and no mode (main.py:216, :223, :236, :261), and collectors use save_json/open with default modes. Under the common umask 022 this gives 0755 folders and 0644 files. Locally, all 4,566 report files are other-readable. shutil.make_archive (main.py:252-255, :278-281) produces plain, unencrypted zips. Recording the operator identity is also legitimate provenance, so this is about defaults and choice rather than a bug. The more sensitive content is the report body itself (IAM policies, secret names, full pod specs).
evidence: main.py:76 `"caller_arn": caller_identity['Arn']`, :77 `"caller_user_id": caller_identity.get('UserId', '')`; os.makedirs without mode at :216/:223/:236/:261; `umask` -> 022; `find reports -type f -perm -o=r | wc -l` -> 4566 of 4566.
impact: On shared jump hosts, other local users can read client enumeration data. The operator's identity travels with every report that is shared with clients or teammates.
fix: Call os.umask(0o077) at the start of main(), or pass mode=0o700 to makedirs and chmod 0600 on writes. Add a --redact-identity flag that hashes or drops caller_arn and caller_user_id. Offer optional encrypted output (pyzipper AES, or pipe to age/gpg), and document secure handling.

title: --region defaults to eu-west-2 and is always passed explicitly, overriding the profile/env region
explanation: parse_args sets default="eu-west-2" (main.py:184), and get_boto3_session passes it as region_name (aws_utils.py:9), so a profile region or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION is ignored. That part is confirmed. However, the default is documented in --help and the README (readme.md:108), and the banner prints "Region: eu-west-2" (main.py:31), so it is not silent. A side effect: with GovCloud/China credentials and no --region, the first STS call (main.py:207) goes to eu-west-2 and fails.
evidence:
main.py:184 `parser.add_argument("--region", default="eu-west-2", ...)`; aws_utils.py:9 `boto3.Session(region_name=region)`.
Repro (env_checks.py): profile region us-west-2 gives plain Session().region_name='us-west-2', while the tool's get_boto3_session('eu-west-2') client region is 'eu-west-2'.
impact: An operator who forgets --region enumerates London regional resources instead of their configured region. Region-scoped data such as EC2, Lambda and secrets may be missing from the graph. The banner shows the region, so the operator can notice.
fix: Default --region to None. Resolve it as args.region or boto3.Session().region_name or 'eu-west-2' (or error), and print where the region came from.

title: Retry env defaults override the user's profile retry config and set a less common UA token; per-item calls keep issuing denied requests; no service scoping
explanation: (1) Config override, confirmed. os.environ.setdefault only checks the environment. botocore resolves env before the config file, so profile retry_mode/max_attempts are silently replaced. (2) UA token, confirmed but weaker than claimed. boto3 always emits a `cfg/retry-mode#<mode>` token, and the default is `legacy`. The tool changes its value to `adaptive`, which is less common, a few extra fingerprint bits. The OS/arch/python fields come from boto3 defaults and are not tool-introduced; any boto3 tool sends them. (3) Per-item AccessDenied bursts, confirmed. No collector short-circuits after an AccessDenied: grep finds no AccessDenied/UnauthorizedOperation handling outside a vpc.py comment. A principal lacking, e.g., iam:ListMFADevices generates one denied CloudTrail event per user (iam.py:113-123), and S3 can generate up to 10 per bucket (s3.py:59-131). (4) No --services/--skip flag, confirmed (main.py:182-190).
impact: Operators lose control of retry behaviour set in their profiles. A detection engineer could key on `cfg/retry-mode#adaptive` together with boto3, but that is a weak signal. The larger OPSEC cost is bursts of AccessDenied events, one per user, bucket or item, with no way to skip noisy collectors. That cost is real for red teams operating against monitored accounts.
fix: Set retry defaults only when neither env nor profile defines them: check boto3.Session().get_config_variable('retry_mode') / 'max_attempts', or pass botocore.config.Config(retries=...) only when they are unset. Add --services/--skip (and --regions) flags. Add a per-collector circuit breaker: after the first AccessDenied for an API, skip that API for the remaining items and record one 'denied' marker. Optionally expose user_agent_extra / AWS_SDK_UA_APP_ID for UA control.

title: Single-account scope; no Organizations/SCP/RCP collection or evaluation
explanation: Each run uses one sts.get_caller_identity() account (main.py:205-209) for the report path and analysis. A grep of app/ for organizations/SCP finds nothing. Permission boundaries are collected (iam.py:139-140, 396-410), but there is no Organizations/SCP/RCP collection or evaluation, and there is no cross-account merge in the dashboard. This is a scope limitation, not a defect, but it does cause over-reporting in member accounts governed by SCPs.
evidence: main.py:205-209 single caller identity and account_number; `grep -rni 'organizations\|scp' app/` returns no matches (only PermissionsBoundary hits in iam.py).
impact: In AWS Organizations member accounts, privesc/dangerous-permission findings may describe actions an SCP or RCP denies, so blue teams see false positives. Org-wide engagements need N separate runs and dashboards with no cross-account trust graph.
fix: Optionally collect organizations:DescribeOrganization, ListPoliciesForTarget and DescribePolicy (SCP/RCP) when permitted, and evaluate Deny statements before emitting findings; at minimum, add a 'may be restricted by SCP' flag when the account is in an org. Longer term, add --org-role to assume a role into each account and let the dashboard merge multiple reports.

title: Sequential execution with per-entity IAM/S3 fan-out and no resume
explanation: The factual claims hold. Regions and modules run strictly sequentially (main.py:231-238). Each IAM user costs 5 calls plus list_user_policies plus get_user_policy per inline policy (iam.py:99-159, 315-333). Each role costs list_attached_role_policies plus list_role_policies plus gets (iam.py:211-220, 335-350). GetAccountAuthorizationDetails is not used. S3 makes 10 Get* calls per bucket (s3.py:59-131), and there is no checkpoint/resume. The point that each client has its own adaptive token bucket is technically true (botocore/retries/adaptive.py:10-25 builds a TokenBucket per client) but moot, because the tool is sequential and never issues concurrent calls. Multi-account support overlaps the Organizations issue. This is slow but correct, so it is re-rated to low; it is a runtime/UX cost, not an accuracy or safety problem.
evidence: main.py:231 `# Sequential regional enumeration`; iam.py:99,114,127,143,151 per-user calls; s3.py:59,66,74,82,90,98,106,114,123,131 ten per-bucket Get* calls; no get_account_authorization_details in app/.
impact: Large accounts take a long time and generate many CloudTrail events (noisy for red teams). A crash late in --all (see the region-discovery issue) loses the run with no resume. Results are not affected.
fix: Use iam:GetAccountAuthorizationDetails (paginated) for users/groups/roles/policies/inline and attached policies, plus the credential report for keys/MFA/login. Run regions in a bounded ThreadPoolExecutor with per-thread sessions. Add --regions/--services filters and a --resume that skips modules whose output already exists for the current run id.

title: --dashboard is unreachable from the Docker image (loopback-only bind, no --host option)
explanation: serve_dashboard binds ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", candidate), ...) (dashboard.py:45). parse_args has only --dashboard and --port (main.py:187-189). Inside a container, Docker's -p forwarding targets the container interface IP, so a loopback-bound server is unreachable from the host, and webbrowser.open (dashboard.py:60) has no browser. One detail is wrong: the missing EXPOSE in the Dockerfile is not a cause. EXPOSE is documentation-only, and -p works without it. Workarounds exist: --network host on Linux, or serving or opening app/dashboard/index.html outside the container, since reports are parsed client-side. The README does not advertise --dashboard with Docker.
evidence: dashboard.py:45 `httpd = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", candidate), handler)`; main.py:187-189 no host flag; Dockerfile:18 `ENTRYPOINT ["python", "app/main.py"]`.
impact: Docker-only operators cannot use the bundled dashboard as documented for pip installs. This is an inconvenience with easy workarounds and has no data-exposure risk.
fix: Add --host (default 127.0.0.1) and document `docker run -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 image --dashboard --host 0.0.0.0`. Skip webbrowser.open when the host is not loopback or no browser is available. Optionally add EXPOSE 8000 as documentation.

title: --port 0 prints and opens http://127.0.0.1:0/ instead of the OS-assigned port; out-of-range ports crash
explanation: After a successful bind the code sets port = candidate (dashboard.py:46) rather than httpd.server_address[1], so with --port 0 the printed and opened URL (dashboard.py:54-60) uses port 0. A related gap: the retry loop catches only OSError, so --port 70000 (or a start near 65535 that walks past it) raises an uncaught OverflowError.
evidence:
Repro (scratchpad/agents/arch-packaging-ci-2/dash.py):
  printed: [+] Serving dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:0/index.html
  opened url: ['http://127.0.0.1:0/index.html'] | actual bound: ('127.0.0.1', 63237)
  port 70000 -> OverflowError bind(): port must be 0-65535.
impact: A minor UX defect: the browser opens a dead URL and the user must find the real port. It affects only users who pass --port 0 or invalid ports.
fix: After binding, set port = httpd.server_address[1]. Validate --port in argparse (0-65535) and catch OverflowError, or clamp the retry range to 65535.

title: Release pipeline publishes :latest on every push to main with no gates; actions, base image and Python deps are unpinned
explanation: Every factual claim checks out. The trigger is push to main with no paths filter, so docs-only commits also publish (:3-5). Both :<version> and :latest are pushed (:50-52). There are no PR builds and no test, lint, image-scan, SBOM, provenance or signing steps. Actions use mutable major tags: actions/checkout@v4 (:22), docker/login-action@v3 (:37), docker/setup-buildx-action@v3 (:43), docker/build-push-action@v6 (:46). The Dockerfile has a floating `FROM python:3.13-slim` (:1). requirements.txt is just `boto3` and `kubernetes`, and kubernetes pulls in many transitive dependencies (urllib3, google-auth, websocket-client, ...); pyproject.toml:23-26 is likewise unpinned. Builds are not reproducible. I rate it low rather than medium: the actions are first-party GitHub and Docker actions, and floating major tags are common practice. The stakes are higher than usual, though, because the image is designed to receive operator AWS credentials. Overlaps with P1-200/P1-178 on the missing test gate.
evidence: docker-publish.yml:3-5, :22, :37, :43, :46, :50-52; Dockerfile:1, :7 `pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt`; requirements.txt: `boto3`, `kubernetes`.
impact: A compromised or broken upstream (PyPI dependency, base image or action tag) reaches the :latest image that operators run with high-privilege AWS credentials, at the next push. Releases cannot be rebuilt or audited byte-for-byte.
fix: Pin actions to commit SHAs (Dependabot can bump them). Pin the base image by digest (python:3.13-slim@sha256:...). Generate a hashed lockfile (pip-compile --generate-hashes or uv lock) and install with --require-hashes. Add a PR workflow with tests, then make publish `needs:` it. Add `paths-ignore: ['**.md','docs/**']`. Add a Trivy or Grype scan, `provenance: true`/`sbom: true` on build-push-action, and cosign signing. Publish :latest only from tags.

title: CI derives PATCH from tag count with no concurrency group and pushes the image before the tag, so version tags can collide and be overwritten
explanation: PATCH=$(git tag -l "v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.*" | wc -l) (:30) is a count, not max+1. The workflow has no `concurrency:` key, and build-push to :<version> and :latest (:45-54) runs before `git tag`/`git push origin <tag>` (:56-61). Two pushes to main in quick succession both see N tags and both push image :0.2.N. Whichever finishes last wins :0.2.N and :latest, so :latest may point at the older commit. The loser's tag push is then rejected because the tag already exists, and the job fails after the image is overwritten, so the image tag 0.2.N and the git tag v0.2.N can point at different commits. If a tag push fails for any reason (e.g. token permissions), the next run recomputes the same N and overwrites the already-published image. Deleting a tag also causes version reuse. Whether `environment: Development` (:18) has protection rules that serialise runs cannot be determined from the repo. Docker Hub tags are mutable by nature, so the impact is limited.
evidence: docker-publish.yml:30 `PATCH=$(git tag -l "v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.*" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')`; :45-54 build-and-push precedes :56-61 tag creation and push; `grep -n concurrency` -> no match.
impact: Released image versions are not immutable or reliably mapped to commits, which weakens reproducibility and incident tracing for users who pin a version.
fix: Add `concurrency: { group: release-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: false }`. Compute the next version as max(existing)+1 with `git tag -l 'v0.2.*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1`, or release only on pushed tags (on: push: tags: ['v*']). Create and push the git tag before pushing the image, failing early if it exists. Push :latest only after the versioned push succeeds.

title: Docker image runs as root, has no .dockerignore, uses a floating base, and ships empty AWS_* ENV placeholders; the README passes credentials with -e KEY=$VAL
explanation: True as stated: there is no USER directive, so the image runs as root, and reports written to a bind mount are root-owned on Linux hosts. FROM python:3.13-slim floats (:1). `VOLUME ["/root/.aws", "${WORK_DIR}/reports"]` (:16) creates anonymous volumes when they are not bind-mounted; without --rm, client reports can linger in /var/lib/docker/volumes. ENTRYPOINT `python app/main.py` (:18) runs in script mode. The package is never pip-installed in the image, so it works only through the ImportError fallbacks in main.py:18-25 and k8s.py:26-29. There is no .dockerignore, but COPY is limited to requirements.txt and app/, so sensitive files enter the build context only, never the image. Narrower than claimed: the empty ENV placeholders at :12-14 are functionally harmless. botocore EnvProvider().load() returns None for empty values, so the provider chain falls through. The credential-exposure risk comes from the README example (readme.md:75-80) passing `-e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, which puts the values on the host docker CLI's argv (visible in ps) and in `docker inspect` Config.Env. It does not come from the Dockerfile ENV lines.
evidence: Dockerfile:1, :11-14, :16, :18; no USER line. `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="" ... python -c 'EnvProvider().load()'` -> None. readme.md:75-80 docker run with `-e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` etc.
impact: Reports produced on Linux bind mounts are root-owned. Operators who follow the README expose temporary credentials to other local users through ps and docker inspect. The image has no reproducible base. The functional risk is low.
fix: Add `RUN useradd -m -u 10001 app` and `USER app`, and mount credentials at /home/app/.aws. Pin the base by digest. `pip install .` in the image and use `ENTRYPOINT ["aws-enumerator"]`. Drop the empty ENV lines. Update the README to use `-e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` (name only, inherited from the environment) or `--env-file`, or a read-only ~/.aws mount with AWS_PROFILE. Add a .dockerignore. Document that --dashboard binds 127.0.0.1 inside the container.

title: Distribution installs a generic top-level package named 'app'
explanation: [tool.setuptools.packages.find] include = ["app*"] (pyproject.toml:35-36), with entry point app.main:main (pyproject.toml:33). The built egg-info top_level.txt is `app`. pip does not detect file conflicts between distributions, so installing this next to any other distribution that ships a top-level `app` package (common in small projects and in images) silently overwrites or shadows modules. pipx or a dedicated venv avoids it.
evidence: pyproject.toml:33 `aws-enumerator = "app.main:main"`; pyproject.toml:36 `include = ["app*"]`; aws_enumerator.egg-info/top_level.txt contains `app`.
impact: Possible breakage of either tool when installed into a shared environment. The scenario is niche and has no security or accuracy impact.
fix: Rename the package to aws_enumerator/ (update imports in main.py and ec2/sg/vpc, the ImportError fallback, the entry point, package-data keys, the Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT and the README tree).

title: Committed README screenshots expose legible, only partly sanitised environment identifiers
evidence: Visual inspection plus a sips crop of a 60x800 region of docs/00.png at the trust-node row: labels of the form 'arn:aws:iam::<12 digits>:root' are readable. docs/01.png detail pane: ARN with a 9s-substituted account. `git log --follow -- docs/0{0,1,2}.png` gives f23b624, 403fad4.
impact: If the environment was a client or employer estate, this permanently discloses its trusted-account map, SSO permission-set naming and key IDs in a public offensive-security repo. Account IDs are not secrets in themselves, but this is an opsec and NDA exposure that helps targeting. If it was a lab, there is no impact.
fix: Regenerate the screenshots from a synthetic or sanitised report: fake 12-digit IDs, generic role and bucket names, and labels hidden or blurred.
